It must be redacted or masked, unless an adequate data protection safeguard is used and verified in the consent request
It may be sent if the foreign preparer holds a PTIN
It must be sent separately
questions.explanation: Reg. § 301.7216-3(b)(4). A US preparer may retransmit an SSN it initially received from that foreign preparer without consent.
questions.pageTitle: Rules for client privacy and consent to disclose

questions.stem: A § 7216 consent says nothing about duration. How long is it effective?
options: Indefinitely
Until the return is filed
One year from the date signed
120 days
questions.explanation: Reg. § 301.7216-3(b)(5) — a consent may specify its duration; where it does not, one year from signature.
questions.pageTitle: Rules for client privacy and consent to disclose

questions.stem: Which may be named on a Form 8821 but not on a Form 2848?
options: An enrolled agent
A certified public accountant
A partnership
An attorney
questions.explanation: Form 8821 authorises any individual, corporation, firm, organization or partnership; Form 2848 names an individual eligible to practise before the IRS.
questions.pageTitle: Distinctions between power of attorney (Form 2848) and tax information authorization (Form 8821)

questions.stem: A Form 8821 designee wants to sign a waiver of restrictions on assessment to close an examination. May he?
options: Yes, if the taxpayer agrees orally
Yes, for years listed on the form
No, Form 8821 does not authorise executing waivers, consents or closing agreements
Yes, if he also holds a CAF number
questions.explanation: The Form 8821 instructions exclude executing waivers, consents and closing agreements, along with speaking for the taxpayer, advocating a position, and representing in any other manner.
questions.pageTitle: Distinctions between power of attorney (Form 2848) and tax information authorization (Form 8821)

questions.stem: A taxpayer files a new Form 2848. What happens to a Form 8821 already on file?
options: It is revoked automatically
It remains in effect
It is suspended until the new power of attorney is recorded
It is converted into a power of attorney
questions.explanation: Filing a Form 2848 does not revoke a Form 8821; the taxpayer must revoke that authorisation separately.
questions.pageTitle: Distinctions between power of attorney (Form 2848) and tax information authorization (Form 8821)

questions.stem: Within what period must the IRS receive a Form 8821 authorising disclosure to a lender for income verification?
options: 30 days from the signature date
60 days from the signature date
120 days from the signature date
No deadline applies
questions.explanation: The 120-day rule applies where the purpose is other than addressing or resolving a tax matter with the IRS; it does not apply where the purpose is assistance with an IRS matter.
questions.pageTitle: Distinctions between power of attorney (Form 2848) and tax information authorization (Form 8821)

questions.stem: May a Form 8821 designee substitute someone else as the taxpayer's designee?
options: Yes, with the taxpayer's oral consent
Yes, if the substitute is also named on the form
No, the designee may never substitute another party
Yes, on the same terms as a Form 2848 representative
questions.explanation: The Form 8821 instructions state it without qualification. Substitution under a Form 2848 is possible but only where the power of attorney specifically permits it.
questions.pageTitle: Distinctions between power of attorney (Form 2848) and tax information authorization (Form 8821)

questions.stem: A taxpayer files a new Form 2848 for the same tax years, naming a different enrolled agent. What is the effect on the earlier authorisation?
options: Both remain in effect
The prior power of attorney is revoked
The prior power remains until the taxpayer files a statement of revocation
The IRS decides which controls
questions.explanation: Reg. § 601.505(a)(1) — a new power of attorney revokes a prior one granted to another recognized representative with respect to the same matter.
questions.pageTitle: Requirements to be met when changing or dropping representatives or withdrawal of representative

questions.stem: What must accompany a new power of attorney if the taxpayer wants to keep the earlier representative?
options: Nothing; naming both on the new form is enough
A non-revocation clause only
A non-revocation clause plus a copy of the prior power or a signed list of its representatives
Written consent of the prior representative
questions.explanation: Reg. § 601.505(a)(1)(i) and (ii) require both the clause and one of the two attachments.
questions.pageTitle: Requirements to be met when changing or dropping representatives or withdrawal of representative

questions.stem: May a recognized representative withdraw without the taxpayer's consent?
options: No, the taxpayer must sign a revocation
Yes, by filing a signed statement identifying the taxpayer and the matters withdrawn from
Only with IRS approval
Only where the fee has been paid
questions.explanation: Reg. § 601.505(b)(1). Circular 230 § 10.28 separately requires the client's records to be returned notwithstanding a fee dispute.
questions.pageTitle: Requirements to be met when changing or dropping representatives or withdrawal of representative

questions.stem: What word does a representative write across the top of the first page of the power of attorney to withdraw, and what must appear below it?
options: REVOKE, with the taxpayer's signature
WITHDRAW, with the representative's current signature and date
CANCEL, with the date only
REMOVE, with both signatures
questions.explanation: The Form 2848 instructions require "WITHDRAW" with a current signature and date below the annotation; "REVOKE" is the taxpayer's annotation for revoking.
questions.pageTitle: Requirements to be met when changing or dropping representatives or withdrawal of representative

questions.stem: Which is not required to effect a substitution of representative?
options: A Notice of Substitution or Delegation
A declaration of representative by the new representative
The written consent of the other representatives appointed for the same matter
A power of attorney specifically authorising the substitution
questions.explanation: Unless the power of attorney provides otherwise, a representative may substitute or delegate without the consent of any other recognized representative appointed in the same matter.
questions.pageTitle: Requirements to be met when changing or dropping representatives or withdrawal of representative

questions.stem: What does issuance of a CAF number establish about the holder?
options: That the holder may practise before the IRS
That the holder is a Circular 230 practitioner
Nothing about eligibility; it facilitates processing of the authorisation
That the holder may receive Treasury checks
questions.explanation: Reg. § 601.506(d)(2) — issuance does not indicate that a person is either recognized or authorized to practise; that is determined under Circular 230.
questions.pageTitle: Purpose of a Centralized Authorization File (CAF) number

questions.stem: A power of attorney received by the IRS in June 2026 covers tax periods through 2033. What is recorded on the CAF?
options: All periods listed
Periods ending no later than 31 December 2029
No periods, because the document spans more than three years
Only periods that have already ended
questions.explanation: The Form 2848 instructions bar recording future periods exceeding 3 years from 31 December of the year of receipt. Reg. § 601.506(d)(3)(ii) measures from the date of receipt; the instructions govern in practice. Either way the document stays valid for the rest and may be resubmitted.
questions.pageTitle: Purpose of a Centralized Authorization File (CAF) number

questions.stem: A Form 2848 names four representatives. What follows?
options: The form is rejected
All four are recorded
The first three are recorded; all four remain appointed
The taxpayer must choose three
questions.explanation: Reg. § 601.506(d)(3)(iv) records no more than three and, where more are named, only the first three. The recording limit does not undo the appointments.
questions.pageTitle: Purpose of a Centralized Authorization File (CAF) number

questions.stem: Which is a "specific use" matter the IRS does not record on the CAF?
options: A 2025 individual income tax examination
A request for a private letter ruling
A 2024 employment tax matter under consideration
A 2026 individual income tax matter
questions.explanation: The Form 2848 instructions list private letter ruling and technical advice requests among specific uses not recorded, along with EIN and ITIN applications, Form 843 claims, corporate dissolutions and Circular 230 disciplinary proceedings — a power of attorney not relating to a specific tax period, except for civil penalties.
questions.pageTitle: Purpose of a Centralized Authorization File (CAF) number

questions.stem: Is an authorisation rejected if the representative omits a CAF number?
options: Yes, it is a substantive requirement
Yes, unless the representative has never been issued one
No, the CAF number is not among the substantive requirements of Reg. § 601.503(a)
No, but only for tax information authorizations
questions.explanation: Reg. § 601.506(d)(2) says a document will not be rejected based on the absence of a CAF number, because the number is not a substantive requirement.
questions.pageTitle: Purpose of a Centralized Authorization File (CAF) number

questions.stem: What constitutes a separate "matter" under Reg. § 601.501(b)(7)?
options: Each taxpayer
Each tax, for each taxable period
Each IRS office involved
Each representative appointed
questions.explanation: Which is why authority must be granted tax by tax and period by period.
questions.pageTitle: Conference and practice requirements (Publication 216)

questions.stem: A representative brings in a colleague under a delegation. Who is recognized afterwards?
options: Only the colleague
Only the original
Both
Neither, until a new form is filed
questions.explanation: Reg. § 601.501(b)(5). After a substitution under § 601.501(b)(14), only the newly recognized representative acts.
questions.pageTitle: Conference and practice requirements (Publication 216)

questions.stem: Two recognized representatives each claim authority over the same matter. What does the IRS do?
options: Recognizes the earlier-filed power
Recognizes the senior practitioner
Recognizes no party until they file an agreement signed by all
Asks the taxpayer to choose
questions.explanation: Reg. § 601.508. The contesting representatives may designate one or more of their number under an agreement signed by all.
questions.pageTitle: Conference and practice requirements (Publication 216)

questions.stem: In which situation is no power of attorney required?
options: Signing a consent to extend the assessment period
An estate tax conference where the individual is § 601.502(b)-eligible and the attorney of record before the probate court
Executing a closing agreement
Representing by correspondence only
questions.explanation: Reg. § 601.504(b)(2) requires both conditions. Correspondence-only representation does require one, under § 601.504(d).
questions.pageTitle: Conference and practice requirements (Publication 216)

questions.stem: A representative is unwilling to declare under penalty of perjury that submitted facts are true. What follows?
options: The submission is rejected
The IRS may require the taxpayer to declare
The representative must withdraw
The evidence is treated as supplementary
questions.explanation: Reg. § 601.507, which also excepts evidence of a supplementary or incidental character from the declaration requirement.
questions.pageTitle: Conference and practice requirements (Publication 216)

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: A client narrates the facts of a transaction and asks for written advice. What does Circular 230 § 10.37 require of the practitioner as to those facts?
options: Accept them as given
Verify every fact independently
Use reasonable efforts to identify and ascertain the facts relevant to the matter
Obtain a client representation letter
questions.explanation: Requirement (iii). A representation letter does not replace reasonable efforts to ascertain.
questions.pageTitle: Identification of tax issue(s) with supporting details

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: May a practitioner take account of the likelihood that a return will not be examined?
options: Yes, as one factor
Yes, for small items
No — Circular 230 § 10.37(a)(2)(vi) forbids it, as does Reg. § 1.6662-4(d)(2)
Only in oral advice
questions.explanation: The prohibition appears in both the practice rules and the penalty regulations.
questions.pageTitle: Identification of tax issue(s) with supporting details

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: Client-supplied information appears inconsistent with an important fact. What must the practitioner do?
options: Rely on it in good faith
Make reasonable inquiries
Withdraw
Disclose to the IRS
questions.explanation: Circular 230 § 10.34(d) permits reliance without verification but not where the information appears incorrect, inconsistent or incomplete.
questions.pageTitle: Identification of tax issue(s) with supporting details

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: When is reliance on another professional's advice unreasonable?
options: Whenever the practitioner could have done the work themselves
Where the practitioner knows or should know the person is not competent, lacks qualifications, or has a Circular 230 conflict
Only where the advice is oral
Never — reliance is always permitted
questions.explanation: Circular 230 § 10.37(b), which also requires the advice itself to have been reasonable and the reliance in good faith.
questions.pageTitle: Identification of tax issue(s) with supporting details

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: A practitioner faces no penalty exposure on a client's position. Must the client still be advised about penalties?
options: No
Only if the client asks
Yes — § 10.34(c) applies even if the practitioner is not subject to a penalty, and the advice must include the disclosure route
Only for positions on returns, not other documents
questions.explanation: It covers documents, affidavits and other papers submitted to the IRS as well as return positions.
questions.pageTitle: Identification of tax issue(s) with supporting details

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: A client's civil examination becomes a criminal investigation. What protection does IRC § 7525 give earlier communications with the enrolled agent?
options: Full protection, since they were made while the matter was civil
None — the privilege may be asserted only in noncriminal matters
Protection unless the IRS shows fraud
Protection only in Federal court
questions.explanation: Both forums in § 7525(a)(2) are limited to noncriminal matters.
questions.pageTitle: Potential for criminal aspects

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: A practitioner learns a client omitted income from a prior return. What does Circular 230 § 10.21 require?
options: Notifying the IRS
Withdrawing from the engagement
Advising the client promptly of the omission and of the consequences under the Code and regulations
Amending the return
questions.explanation: The duty runs to the client, and § 10.21 requires nothing beyond it.
questions.pageTitle: Potential for criminal aspects

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: What is the effect of a Justice Department referral under IRC § 7602(d)?
options: The examination must close
No summons may be issued and no § 7604 enforcement action begun as to that person
The limitation period is suspended
The taxpayer must be notified
questions.explanation: And each taxable period and separately-imposed tax is treated separately.
questions.pageTitle: Potential for criminal aspects

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: When may the IRS use financial status or economic reality examination techniques to determine the existence of unreported income?
options: At any time during an examination
Only with the taxpayer's consent
Only where there is a reasonable indication that unreported income is likely
Only in a criminal investigation
questions.pageTitle: Potential for criminal aspects

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: Which of these ends a Justice Department referral?
options: The passage of one year
The examiner closing the civil case
Written notification from the Attorney General declining prosecution or a grand jury investigation, or final disposition of a criminal proceeding
The taxpayer filing an amended return
questions.explanation: IRC § 7602(d)(2)(B), and the notification must be in writing.
questions.pageTitle: Potential for criminal aspects

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: An enrolled agent is engaged on a matter in an unfamiliar area. What does Circular 230 § 10.35 require?
options: The agent must decline
The agent must refer the matter to an attorney
The agent must possess the necessary competence, which may be acquired by consulting experts or studying the relevant law
The agent may proceed without further preparation
questions.explanation: Competence is measured for the matter engaged on, and the rule expressly contemplates acquiring it.
questions.pageTitle: Competence, expertise and time to handle issue

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: Which of these is within the § 10.22 due diligence duty?
options: Only returns and documents filed with the IRS
Only written representations
Also determining the correctness of oral or written representations made to clients on matters administered by the IRS
Only representations made to Treasury
questions.explanation: There are three limbs, and the one covering advice to clients is the most easily forgotten.
questions.pageTitle: Competence, expertise and time to handle issue

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: A practitioner relies on work performed by a staff member. When is due diligence presumed?
options: Always, where the work is delegated
Where the practitioner used reasonable care in engaging, supervising, training and evaluating that person
Never — delegation does not satisfy diligence
Only where the staff member is credentialed
questions.explanation: Reliance plus reasonable care; the presumption is modified by §§ 10.34 and 10.37.
questions.pageTitle: Competence, expertise and time to handle issue

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: A new client provides the prior year's return prepared by another enrolled agent. What does due diligence require?
options: No review at all
Review for reasonable accuracy — the prior preparer's work is not presumed wrong
A complete re-audit as though the practitioner had prepared it
That it not be used as a reference
questions.explanation: But reliance stops being reasonable where something on the face of the return should prompt a question.
questions.pageTitle: Competence, expertise and time to handle issue

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: What must exist before an individual with principal authority over a firm's practice is disciplined under § 10.36(b)?
options: Any compliance failure at the firm
Willfulness, recklessness or gross incompetence, together with a pattern or practice of non-compliance
A referral from OPR
A conviction
questions.explanation: Both elements are required; a single incident is not enough.
questions.pageTitle: Competence, expertise and time to handle issue

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: Which of these is a conflict of interest under Circular 230 § 10.29?
options: Only where two current clients are directly adverse
Also where a significant risk exists that representation will be materially limited by duties to a former client, a third person, or the practitioner's personal interest
Only where the clients are related
Only where the practitioner is paid by one of them
questions.explanation: The second limb reaches former clients, non-clients and the practitioner's own interest.
questions.pageTitle: Conflict of interest in regards to representation

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: What must accompany a client's waiver of a conflict?
options: Nothing further
Oral informed consent
Informed consent confirmed in writing by each affected client, no later than 30 days
Approval from the Office of Professional Responsibility
questions.explanation: And the practitioner must also reasonably believe competent and diligent representation of each is possible, and the representation must not be prohibited by law.
questions.pageTitle: Conflict of interest in regards to representation

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: How long must written consents be retained?
options: 12 months from the date of consent
30 days
At least 36 months from the conclusion of the representation of the affected clients
Indefinitely
questions.explanation: And they must be provided to any IRS officer or employee on request.
questions.pageTitle: Conflict of interest in regards to representation

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: A practitioner cannot honestly believe they can act competently and diligently for both clients, but both give written informed consent. May the practitioner act?
options: Yes — consent cures the conflict
Yes, if the consents are retained
No — all three conditions in § 10.29(b) must be satisfied
Yes, with OPR approval
questions.explanation: Consent is one condition of three, not a substitute for the others.
questions.pageTitle: Conflict of interest in regards to representation

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: When does the obligation to address a conflict arise?
options: At engagement, always
At the time the existence of the conflict is known by the practitioner
When the IRS raises it
When the client objects
questions.explanation: Which is usually mid-engagement, as facts emerge.
questions.pageTitle: Conflict of interest in regards to representation

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: Which transcript shows changes made to an account after the original return was filed?
options: Tax return transcript
Tax account transcript
Wage and income transcript
Verification of non-filing letter
questions.explanation: The tax return transcript shows the return as filed and does not show later changes.
questions.pageTitle: Transcripts from IRS (e.g., access to and use of e-services)

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: What does a verification of non-filing letter establish?
options: That the taxpayer was not required to file
That the IRS has no record of a processed Form 1040-series return as of the request date
That the taxpayer filed late
That the statute has expired
questions.explanation: It expressly does not indicate whether a return was required.
questions.pageTitle: Transcripts from IRS (e.g., access to and use of e-services)

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: A client with many payers requests a wage and income transcript online and it will not generate. Why?
options: The year is too old
The transcript is limited to approximately 85 income documents
No authorisation is on file
The account is under examination
questions.explanation: The fallback is Form 4506-T.
questions.pageTitle: Transcripts from IRS (e.g., access to and use of e-services)

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: What must be on file before a practitioner may use the Transcript Delivery System for a client?
options: Nothing beyond the practitioner's credential
A properly executed Form 2848 or Form 8821
A Form 4506
A signed engagement letter
questions.explanation: TDS is open to EROs and Circular 230 practitioners, but the authorisation must already be on file.
questions.pageTitle: Transcripts from IRS (e.g., access to and use of e-services)

questions.sectionTitle: Building the taxpayer’s case - Preliminary work
questions.stem: A client needs an actual copy of a filed return for a court. What is requested?
options: A tax return transcript
A record of account transcript
Form 4506, Request for Copy of Tax Return
Form 4506-T
questions.explanation: A transcript is not a photocopy; Form 4506 carries a fee and a processing time.
questions.pageTitle: Transcripts from IRS (e.g., access to and use of e-services)

questions.stem: A Collection Information Statement is ordinarily supported by income and spending documentation covering what period?
options: The prior three months
The prior six months
The prior twelve months in every case
The full period since the balance arose
questions.explanation: Wage statements for the prior three months and cancelled checks and credit card statements for the last three months are the ordinary review, though additional months up to one year may be reviewed where three are not representative.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer's ability to pay the tax

questions.stem: Which of the following does not suspend the collection statute expiration date?
options: A bankruptcy case
A pending collection due process hearing
Currently not collectible status
A continuous absence from the United States of at least six months
questions.explanation: Hardship status halts collection activity but has no statutory suspension provision; the clock continues to run while the account sits.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer's ability to pay the tax

questions.stem: A taxpayer has an installment agreement in effect and is making payments on time. What is the effect on the collection period?
options: It is suspended for as long as the agreement is in effect
It continues to run
It is suspended for the first year only
It is extended by the length of the agreement automatically
questions.explanation: Levy is prohibited while an agreement is in effect, but the statutory suspension that accompanies the other levy prohibitions is expressly withheld from that one period.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer's ability to pay the tax

questions.stem: A taxpayer pays car insurance twice a year. How is it entered on the financial statement?
options: In the months the premium is actually paid
Only if the vehicle is required for employment
Averaged over twelve months
It is covered by the transportation standard and not listed
questions.explanation: Necessary living expenses with varying monthly payments are totalled for the year and divided by twelve.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer's ability to pay the tax

questions.stem: A taxpayer with almost no disposable income owns unencumbered land she does not use, worth more than the balance owed. What should the representative expect?
options: An offer in compromise will be accepted because monthly income is insufficient
The equity will have to be addressed before other collection alternatives are considered
The land is disregarded because it produces no income
Hardship status follows automatically from the low disposable income
questions.explanation: Where equity in assets equals or exceeds the liability and the asset can be sold or borrowed against without hardship, full payment is requested before alternatives are considered.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer's ability to pay the tax

questions.stem: A taxpayer's liabilities immediately before a credit card settlement exceed the fair market value of their assets by 12,000 dollars. The settlement discharges 20,000 dollars. How much may be excluded from gross income on insolvency grounds?
options: Nothing, because insolvency is not an exclusion
12,000 dollars
20,000 dollars
8,000 dollars
questions.explanation: The exclusion may not exceed the amount by which the taxpayer is insolvent, measured immediately before the discharge.
questions.pageTitle: General financial health

questions.stem: A taxpayer owns a rental property jointly with a sibling and cannot document their respective contributions. How will the equity be allocated?
options: Entirely to the taxpayer, as the liable party
Equally between the owners
Entirely to the non-liable owner
In proportion to the rental income each reports
questions.explanation: Equity in jointly held assets is allocated equally unless the joint owners demonstrate that their interests are different.
questions.pageTitle: General financial health

questions.stem: Which statement about property exempt from levy is correct?
options: The exemption releases the federal tax lien on that property
Exempt property is excluded from an offer in compromise computation
The exemption restricts levy but leaves the lien in place
Exempt property may never be sold while a balance is owed
questions.explanation: The statutory list limits what a levy may reach; it does not release the lien, and the lien follows the proceeds on a voluntary sale.
questions.pageTitle: General financial health

questions.stem: A business cannot pay its delinquent balance now but projects improving revenue over the next year. What does the Financial Analysis Handbook contemplate?
options: Immediate enforced collection, because current ability to pay is absent
An installment agreement with increasing payments as cash flow improves
Automatic acceptance of an offer in compromise
Referral to bankruptcy counsel
questions.explanation: Cash flow projections are used precisely to decide whether a business can meet current obligations and retire the arrears, and a graduated agreement is the IRM's own example.
questions.pageTitle: General financial health

questions.stem: A taxpayer excludes discharge-of-indebtedness income under the insolvency exclusion. What follows?
options: Nothing further; the amount is permanently forgiven for tax purposes
The excluded amount is added back over five years
The excluded amount reduces tax attributes such as losses, credits and basis
The taxpayer must file an amended return for the prior year
questions.explanation: The exclusion is applied to reduce tax attributes, so the benefit is deferred rather than cancelled.
questions.pageTitle: General financial health

questions.stem: According to the Financial Analysis Handbook, what does a revenue officer do before requesting supporting documents from the taxpayer?
options: Issue a summons to the taxpayer's bank
Verify as much of the statement as possible through internal sources and online research
Contact the taxpayer's employer for a wage verification
Refer the case for a field examination
questions.explanation: Documents are requested from the taxpayer where internal locator services are unavailable or a discrepancy is indicated, not as the first step.
questions.pageTitle: Third-party research

questions.stem: A representative finds the client's home titled to a single-member LLC on the county assessment roll. What is the correct treatment on a Collection Information Statement?
options: Omit it, because the LLC and not the client owns the property
Disclose it; a single-member LLC is disregarded and the equity belongs to the client
Disclose it only if the revenue officer asks
Disclose the LLC but not the property
questions.explanation: The IRM directs checking assessment records for ownership in business names precisely because this arrangement is common, and omission reads as concealment.
questions.pageTitle: Third-party research

questions.stem: Which is the best use of a municipal property tax assessment record?
options: Establishing fair market value for an offer computation
Establishing ownership and locating undisclosed property
Establishing the priority of a federal tax lien
Establishing the taxpayer's monthly housing expense
questions.explanation: Assessment ratios vary too widely between jurisdictions for the assessed figure to serve as value, but ownership of record is reliable.
questions.pageTitle: Third-party research

questions.stem: A client's Form 433 claims a monthly mortgage payment, but none of the supplied bank statements shows it being paid. What should the representative expect?
options: The expense will be allowed because it is a local standard category
A request for proof of payment, on the view that an undisclosed account may exist
The statement will be accepted as filed
The mortgage will be treated as forgiven debt
questions.explanation: Comparing claimed expenses against payments actually made from disclosed accounts is an express step, and an unexplained gap points to an undisclosed account.
questions.pageTitle: Third-party research

questions.stem: A client filed FinCEN Form 114 for a prior year. What follows for the financial analysis?
options: Nothing; the report is filed with FinCEN and is invisible to collection
Research through the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network Query, and FATCA research where
The foreign account is automatically excluded from the equity computation
The case is referred for criminal investigation
questions.explanation: The filing signals a reportable foreign financial interest, and the handbook directs both FinCEN query research and FATCA research where indicators are present.
questions.pageTitle: Third-party research

questions.stem: An individual with an unpaid assessed income tax liability files a bankruptcy petition. What is the immediate effect on IRS collection?
options: The liability is cancelled on filing
An automatic stay halts assessment and collection until the stay is lifted or the case ends
Collection continues unless the debtor obtains a court order
The IRS receives an automatic one-year extension of the collection period
questions.explanation: The stay arises by operation of the filing itself; nothing has to be requested.
questions.pageTitle: Discharge of the tax liability in bankruptcy

questions.stem: A taxpayer filed a return on time under an extension that ran to 15 October. For the three-year priority test, the period is measured from which date?
options: The original April due date
15 October, the date the return was last due including extensions
The date the return was actually filed
The date the tax was assessed
questions.explanation: Section 507(a)(8)(A)(i) counts from when the return is last due, including extensions.
questions.pageTitle: Discharge of the tax liability in bankruptcy

questions.stem: A taxpayer never filed returns for three years and the IRS prepared substitutes for return. Ten years later the taxpayer files chapter 7. What happens to those liabilities?
options: They are discharged because all the time periods have run
They are excepted from discharge because no return was filed or given
They are discharged only if the IRS failed to file a proof of claim
They are discharged two years after the substitutes were prepared
questions.explanation: The exception for tax on which a required return was not filed or given has no expiry, and the discharge exception does not depend on a proof of claim.
questions.pageTitle: Discharge of the tax liability in bankruptcy

questions.stem: Which liability cannot be discharged in either chapter 7 or a completed chapter 13 plan?
options: Income tax for a year whose return was filed on time eight years before the petition
A penalty for late payment on an old dischargeable year
Withheld employment tax for which the debtor is liable
Income tax assessed 300 days before the petition on a timely old return
questions.explanation: Tax required to be collected or withheld is priority under § 507(a)(8)(C) and is named expressly in the chapter 13 discharge exceptions.
questions.pageTitle: Discharge of the tax liability in bankruptcy

questions.stem: A debtor receives a discharge of an income tax liability. A Notice of Federal Tax Lien was properly filed before the petition and was not avoided. What is the result?
options: The lien is extinguished with the debt
Personal liability is discharged, but the lien continues to encumber pre-petition property
The lien attaches to property acquired after the discharge
The lien survives only if the IRS filed a proof of claim
questions.explanation: The discharge enjoins collection of the debt as a personal liability; a properly filed tax lien continues against the property it attached to before the case.
questions.pageTitle: Discharge of the tax liability in bankruptcy

questions.stem: A taxpayer with a household of three reports actual monthly spending of 1,400 dollars on food, clothing, housekeeping supplies, personal care and miscellaneous. The three-person national standard for those categories is higher than that. What amount is allowed?
options: 1,400 dollars, because allowances are limited to amounts actually spent
The full three-person national standard
The average of actual spending and the standard
1,400 dollars unless the taxpayer substantiates the difference
questions.explanation: National standards are allowed in full for the family size without questioning the amounts actually spent, and the IRM's own example allows the standard where actual spending is lower.
questions.pageTitle: IRS Collection Financial Standards

questions.stem: Which pair of Collection Financial Standards is established on a local rather than a national basis?
options: Food and clothing
Out-of-pocket health care and food
Housing and utilities, and transportation
Transportation and out-of-pocket health care
questions.explanation: Housing and utilities are set by county and family size; transportation operating costs are set by Census region and metropolitan area. Both are ceilings, not entitlements.
questions.pageTitle: IRS Collection Financial Standards

questions.stem: A taxpayer owns a vehicle outright with no loan or lease payment. What transportation allowance applies?
options: Ownership plus operating costs, as for any vehicle owner
The operating cost portion only
The public transportation allowance only
Nothing, because there is no payment to allow
questions.explanation: With no lease or loan payment the allowable ownership cost is zero, and only the operating component of the transportation standard is used.
questions.pageTitle: IRS Collection Financial Standards

questions.stem: A taxpayer cannot full-pay within six years and claims a conditional expense that does not meet the necessary expense test. Which is correct?
options: The expense must be disallowed immediately, because the six-year rule does not apply
The taxpayer may be given up to one year to modify or eliminate the expense
Conditional expenses are never allowed under any circumstances
The expense is allowed in full because the six-year rule was not met
questions.explanation: The one-year rule allows up to a year to modify or eliminate excessive necessary expenses, and the taxpayer need not qualify for the six-year rule in order to use it.
questions.pageTitle: IRS Collection Financial Standards

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a category of Collection Financial Standard?
options: Transportation
Out-of-pocket health care expenses
Employment
Housing and utilities
questions.explanation: The four categories are food/clothing/other items, out-of-pocket health care, housing and utilities, and transportation. There is no employment standard.
questions.pageTitle: IRS Collection Financial Standards

questions.stem: Which category is not subject to the strict substantiation rules of IRC § 274(d)?
options: Traveling expenses including meals and lodging while away from home
Expenses for gifts
Office supplies purchased locally
Listed property
questions.explanation: Ordinary supplies fall under the general § 6001 regime, where approximation and reconstruction are available.
questions.pageTitle: Financial documents and expense records

questions.stem: What does § 274(d) require the taxpayer to substantiate for each covered item?
options: Amount only
Amount and business purpose only
Amount; time and place of travel or date and description of the gift; business purpose; and the
Amount, and the identity of the payee
questions.pageTitle: Financial documents and expense records

questions.stem: What constitutes "adequate records" for § 274(d) purposes?
options: A bank statement showing the payment
An account book, diary, log, statement of expense, trip sheet or similar record, together with
The taxpayer's signed statement of the expense
A summary schedule prepared at the time the return is filed
questions.explanation: The record and the receipt need not duplicate each other so long as they complement each other in an orderly manner.
questions.pageTitle: Financial documents and expense records

questions.stem: A taxpayer prepares a log after the year has ended. What is the evidentiary consequence?
options: It is disregarded entirely
It is treated as adequate records
It may serve as the taxpayer's own statement, but the corroborating evidence must have a high
It shifts the burden of proof to the IRS
questions.pageTitle: Financial documents and expense records

questions.stem: A cancelled cheque establishes which element of a business expense?
options: That the amount was paid, and to whom
The business purpose of the payment
The business relationship of the payee
All required elements
questions.explanation: Purpose and relationship must come from other evidence.
questions.pageTitle: Financial documents and expense records

questions.stem: A divorce decree awards the dependency claim to the noncustodial parent. What else is required?
options: Nothing; the decree is sufficient
A signed written declaration from the custodial parent, attached to the noncustodial parent's return
A court order directed to the IRS
A copy of the child's birth certificate attached to the return
questions.explanation: Form 8332 is that declaration.
questions.pageTitle: Legal documents

questions.stem: Which is excluded from gross income under IRC § 104(a)(2)?
options: Punitive damages awarded in a personal injury suit
Compensatory damages received on account of personal physical injuries
Damages for emotional distress not attributable to physical injury
Back pay in an employment settlement
questions.explanation: Punitive damages are expressly excluded from the exclusion, and emotional distress unconnected to physical injury does not qualify.
questions.pageTitle: Legal documents

questions.stem: For which instruments was the alimony deduction repealed?
options: All instruments, from 2018 onward
Instruments executed after 31 December 2018, and earlier instruments modified afterwards where the
Only instruments executed after 31 December 2025
Instruments where the payments exceed a stated annual amount
questions.pageTitle: Legal documents

questions.stem: What does a birth certificate establish for dependency purposes?
options: Relationship and age
Support
Residency for more than half the year
All of the dependency tests
questions.explanation: Support and residency require separate evidence.
questions.pageTitle: Legal documents

questions.stem: A settlement agreement recites a single sum with no allocation between a physical injury claim and a retaliation claim. How is the character determined?
options: The whole amount is excluded
The whole amount is included
From the underlying claim, the pleadings and the negotiation record
Half is excluded by default
questions.explanation: which is why an allocation negotiated in the agreement itself is worth obtaining.
questions.pageTitle: Legal documents

questions.stem: A preparer relies on a carryover figure from a previously filed return. What must the preparer confirm?
options: That the taxpayer's copy matches the filed original
That the position relied upon has not been adjusted by examination or otherwise
That the prior preparer was credentialed
Nothing; reliance on a filed return is unqualified
questions.pageTitle: Prior and subsequent tax returns

questions.stem: A preparer prepares an amended return. What is the position on the original return's items?
options: Every item must be independently verified
The preparer may rely in good faith without verifying the original's positions, subject to the
The original must be re-created from source documents
The preparer may not prepare an amended return for a return they did not prepare
questions.pageTitle: Prior and subsequent tax returns

questions.stem: Why do subsequent returns matter in an examination of an earlier year?
options: They are irrelevant; each year stands alone
They show whether a treatment was repeated, whether a carryover was used, and whether a method was
They automatically extend the assessment period
They must be produced whenever the earlier year is examined
questions.pageTitle: Prior and subsequent tax returns

questions.stem: An adjustment in the examined year produces an overpayment in an earlier year. What limits the recovery?
options: Nothing; correlative adjustments are automatic
The IRC § 6511 period for that year — three years from filing or two from payment, whichever is
The collection statute for the examined year
A six-year period in all cases
questions.pageTitle: Prior and subsequent tax returns

questions.stem: Which is an element of the normal office practice the preparer penalty regulation rewards?
options: Owning current software
A review of the prior year's return
Retaining returns for six years
Employing a credentialed reviewer
questions.explanation: along with checklists, methods for obtaining information from the taxpayer, and review procedures.
questions.pageTitle: Prior and subsequent tax returns

questions.stem: By when must a contemporaneous written acknowledgment be obtained?
options: Before the IRS opens an examination
By the earlier of the date the return is filed or the due date including extensions
Within one year of the contribution
At any time before the assessment period expires
questions.pageTitle: Other substantive and contemporaneous documentation

questions.stem: Which is not a required content item of the acknowledgment?
options: The amount of cash contributed
Whether the organization provided goods or services in consideration
The value of any non-cash property contributed
A good faith estimate of the value of any goods or services provided
questions.explanation: The acknowledgment describes non-cash property but does not value it — valuation is the donor's responsibility.
questions.pageTitle: Other substantive and contemporaneous documentation

questions.stem: A taxpayer's mileage log is prepared after year end. What follows under § 274(d)?
options: The deduction is automatically disallowed
The log qualifies as adequate records
It may serve as the taxpayer's own statement, but the corroborating evidence must have a high degree
The burden shifts to the IRS
questions.pageTitle: Other substantive and contemporaneous documentation

questions.stem: A client asks the practitioner to prepare a log dated as of the prior year. What is the correct response?
options: Prepare it, since the underlying facts are true
Prepare it and note in the file that it was created later
Refuse; prepare a current-dated statement identifying the corroborating evidence instead
Prepare it only if the client signs a representation
questions.explanation: A document created later and dated earlier is a false document.
questions.pageTitle: Other substantive and contemporaneous documentation

questions.stem: What is the primary tax value of contemporaneous corporate minutes?
options: They satisfy IRC § 274(d) for entity travel
They evidence authorisation and purpose at the time a decision was made
They extend the assessment period
They substitute for a written acknowledgment of a corporate charitable gift
questions.pageTitle: Other substantive and contemporaneous documentation

questions.stem: A domestic limited liability company with two members files no classification election. How is it classified?
options: As a corporation
As a partnership
As disregarded from its owners
It may not operate until an election is filed
questions.explanation: A single-owner domestic eligible entity that files no election is disregarded.
questions.pageTitle: Business entity supporting documents

questions.stem: An operating agreement states that the company will be taxed as a corporation. No Form 8832 is filed. What is the classification?
options: A corporation, as the agreement provides
The default classification for the entity, because the agreement does not make an election
Undetermined until the IRS rules
A partnership in every case
questions.explanation: Classification comes from a filed election or the default rules.
questions.pageTitle: Business entity supporting documents

questions.stem: A partnership agreement allocates depreciation entirely to one partner, but capital accounts were never maintained. How is the distributive share determined?
options: As the agreement provides, in all cases
Equally among the partners
In accordance with the partner's interest in the partnership, taking into account all facts and
By the partnership representative's election
questions.explanation: An allocation under the agreement governs only if it has substantial economic effect.
questions.pageTitle: Business entity supporting documents

questions.stem: A Form 8832 is filed without the entity's taxpayer identifying number. What is the effect?
options: The election is effective when the number is later supplied
The election will not be accepted
The election is effective but subject to penalty
The IRS assigns a number and processes the election
questions.explanation: The regulation conditions acceptance on all required information being provided.
questions.pageTitle: Business entity supporting documents

questions.stem: A foreign eligible entity has two members, both of whom have limited liability, and files no election. How is it classified?
options: As a partnership
As an association
As disregarded from its owners
It has no classification until an election is filed
questions.explanation: The foreign default turns on limited liability rather than on the number of members.
questions.pageTitle: Business entity supporting documents

questions.stem: How long does a temporary regulation last?
options: Indefinitely, until finalised
One year
It expires within 3 years after the date of issuance
Until the next Treasury decision
questions.explanation: IRC § 7805(e)(2), which also requires that any temporary regulation be issued as a proposed regulation.
questions.pageTitle: Internal Revenue Code and income tax regulations

questions.stem: What weight does a proposed regulation carry?
options: The same as a final regulation
None at all
It binds no one, but is authority for the substantial authority analysis
It binds the IRS but not taxpayers
questions.explanation: Reg. § 1.6662-4(d)(3)(iii) lists proposed, temporary and final regulations.
questions.pageTitle: Internal Revenue Code and income tax regulations

questions.stem: A regulation is filed with the Federal Register in March 2026. May it apply to a taxable period ending in 2024?
options: Always — regulations are retroactive to the date of the statute
Generally not, unless an exception in IRC § 7805(b) applies
Only with the taxpayer's consent
Only if it is a temporary regulation
questions.explanation: The exceptions include regulations filed or issued within 18 months of enactment of the statute, prevention of abuse, and correction of a procedural defect.
questions.pageTitle: Internal Revenue Code and income tax regulations

questions.stem: Reg. § 301.7605-1 belongs to which body of regulations?
options: Income tax
Estate tax
Procedure and administration
The Statement of Procedural Rules
questions.explanation: Part 1 is income tax, part 20 estate, part 25 gift, part 601 the Statement of Procedural Rules.
questions.pageTitle: Internal Revenue Code and income tax regulations

questions.stem: Under IRC § 7805(f), who reviews a proposed or temporary regulation for its impact on small business?
options: The Joint Committee on Taxation
The Chief Counsel for Advocacy of the Small Business Administration
The Taxpayer Advocate
The Office of Management and Budget
questions.explanation: Comments are due within 4 weeks and must be considered before a superseding final regulation is prescribed.
questions.pageTitle: Internal Revenue Code and income tax regulations

questions.stem: Which best describes a revenue procedure?
options: An official interpretation of the law applied to stated facts
A statement of procedure affecting rights or duties under the Code, or information that should be a matter of public knowledge
A ruling issued to a single taxpayer
An internal management document that is never published
questions.explanation: The interpretation of law applied to stated facts is a revenue ruling.
questions.pageTitle: Revenue rulings and revenue procedures

questions.stem: What weight does a published revenue ruling carry?
options: The force and effect of a Treasury regulation
None — it binds no one
Less than a regulation, but it is a precedent that may be cited and relied on
Binding on the courts
questions.explanation: Reg. § 601.601(d)(2)(v)(d), which also bars any IRS officer or employee from citing an unpublished ruling as precedent.
questions.pageTitle: Revenue rulings and revenue procedures

questions.stem: When may a taxpayer rely on a published revenue ruling for their own transaction?
options: Always
Only after obtaining a private letter ruling applying it
Where the facts and circumstances are substantially the same, having considered subsequent developments
Only in the year the ruling was issued
questions.explanation: Each ruling is the Service's conclusion on the entire state of facts involved.
questions.pageTitle: Revenue rulings and revenue procedures

questions.stem: A revenue ruling is silent about IRC § 7805(b). Does it apply retroactively?
options: No — retroactivity requires an express statement
Yes — rulings apply retroactively unless the ruling states the extent to which they do not
Only to open years
Only if the taxpayer elects
questions.explanation: Invoking § 7805(b) to limit retroactivity requires an affirmative action.
questions.pageTitle: Revenue rulings and revenue procedures

questions.stem: Which is published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin alongside rulings and procedures?
options: Private letter rulings issued to individual taxpayers
Internal training materials
The Commissioner's acquiescences and nonacquiescences in Tax Court decisions other than memorandum opinions
Examination workpapers
questions.explanation: Along with Treasury decisions, Executive orders, tax conventions, legislation and court decisions.
questions.pageTitle: Revenue rulings and revenue procedures

questions.stem: A Tax Court decision goes against the IRS. What must the IRS do for other taxpayers?
options: Follow it nationwide
Nothing — a lower court decision binds it only for that taxpayer and those years
Issue a revenue ruling
Appeal it
questions.explanation: IRM 4.10.7.2.8.8. Only Supreme Court decisions bind the Service generally.
questions.pageTitle: Case law

questions.stem: Which Tax Court decisions have no precedential value?
options: Regular opinions
Memorandum decisions
Decisions under the small tax case procedures
All Tax Court decisions
questions.explanation: They are also final and may not be appealed by either party.
questions.pageTitle: Case law

questions.stem: What does "acquiescence in result only" mean?
options: The IRS rejects the decision entirely
The IRS accepts the holding but signals disagreement or concern with some or all of the court's reasoning
The IRS will follow the decision only in the deciding circuit
The decision is under appeal
questions.explanation: Plain "acquiescence" indicates neither approval nor disapproval of the court's reasons.
questions.pageTitle: Case law

questions.stem: May an Action on Decision be cited as precedent?
options: Yes, once published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin
Yes, by IRS personnel only
No — but it is still on the Reg. § 1.6662-4 authority list if issued after 12 March 1981
No, and it is not authority in any sense
questions.explanation: It is not an affirmative statement of IRS position and is not intended as public guidance.
questions.pageTitle: Case law

questions.stem: In which forum may a taxpayer request a jury trial?
options: The U.S. Tax Court
The U.S. Court of Federal Claims
A U.S. District Court
Any of the three
questions.explanation: It is the only court where a jury may be requested, and it requires full payment and a refund claim first.
questions.pageTitle: Case law

questions.stem: May an IRS publication be cited to sustain a position on examination?
options: Yes — it is IRS guidance
Yes, if current for the tax year
No — the IRS instructs its own examiners that publications should not be cited to sustain a position
Yes, but only in Appeals
questions.explanation: IRM 4.10.7.2.7. Publications are nonbinding and do not necessarily cover all positions for an issue.
questions.pageTitle: IRS forms, instructions and publications

questions.stem: A taxpayer follows an IRS publication that turns out to misstate the law. What is the effect on the tax?
options: The publication controls
The law controls the taxpayer's liability
The tax is abated automatically
The IRS is estopped from collecting
questions.explanation: Only guidance published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin has precedential value.
questions.pageTitle: IRS forms, instructions and publications

questions.stem: Same taxpayer, and an accuracy-related penalty is proposed. What is the argument?
options: None — the position was wrong
Reasonable good-faith reliance on the publication, which answers a penalty carrying a reasonable cause standard
That the publication is authority
That the IRS must abate under § 6404(f)
questions.explanation: Reg. § 1.6664-4(b), and the IRS states this expressly for forms, instructions, publications and webpages.
questions.pageTitle: IRS forms, instructions and publications

questions.stem: Which FAQs count as authority for the substantial authority exception?
options: All FAQs on IRS.gov
None
FAQs published in a Fact Sheet linked to an IRS news release
FAQs more than one year old
questions.explanation: FAQs not published in the Bulletin will not be cited as precedent by Service personnel.
questions.pageTitle: IRS forms, instructions and publications

questions.stem: What does IRC § 6404(f) require before a penalty attributable to erroneous IRS advice is abated?
options: Any IRS advice the taxpayer relied on
Written advice given in response to a written request, reasonably relied on, with adequate and accurate information supplied
Advice from a revenue agent
A private letter ruling
questions.explanation: A telephone answer does not qualify, however clear it was.
questions.pageTitle: IRS forms, instructions and publications

questions.stem: Which statement about a private letter ruling is NOT true?
options: The request carries no fee
It binds the IRS as to the taxpayer who requested it, on the facts represented
It is published with identifying details removed
It rests on the specific facts the taxpayer supplied
questions.explanation: IRC § 7528 requires user fees, payable in advance and varying by category of request.
questions.pageTitle: Private letter ruling

questions.stem: To whom may a private letter ruling be applied?
options: As precedent in similar cases
As precedent in cases the IRS determines are identical
Only to the taxpayer who requested it, on the facts presented
To anyone, as a non-binding suggestion
questions.explanation: IRC § 6110(k)(3) bars its use as precedent, and it binds the Service only as to the requester.
questions.pageTitle: Private letter ruling

questions.stem: A practitioner finds a 2018 private letter ruling issued to an unrelated taxpayer supporting a position. What is its status?
options: Binding on the IRS
Authority for the substantial authority weighing, but not citable as precedent
Not authority at all
Authority only if the facts are identical
questions.explanation: It is on the Reg. § 1.6662-4(d)(3)(iii) list as a PLR issued after 31 October 1976.
questions.pageTitle: Private letter ruling

questions.stem: When will the IRS not issue a determination letter?
options: Where the taxpayer has not paid the fee
Where the question is novel or cannot be answered on clearly established rules
Where the taxpayer is under examination
Where the amount at stake is small
questions.explanation: Reg. § 601.201(a)(3). A novel question needs a ruling from the National Office.
questions.pageTitle: Private letter ruling

questions.stem: A taxpayer obtains a ruling and then carries out the transaction with a materially different feature. What happens to the substantial authority the ruling gave?
options: It survives unchanged
It survives if the change was inadvertent
It is lost — the protection does not apply where the facts that subsequently develop are materially different
It survives until the IRS revokes the ruling
questions.explanation: Reg. § 1.6662-4(d)(3)(iv)(A), which also withdraws it for a misstatement or omission of a material fact.
questions.pageTitle: Private letter ruling

questions.stem: What is the status of the Internal Revenue Manual as authority?
options: It has the force of a Treasury regulation
It is on the Reg. § 1.6662-4 authority list
It is not authority and confers no rights on taxpayers
It binds taxpayers but not the IRS
questions.explanation: It is the IRS's instructions to its own staff.
questions.pageTitle: Internal Revenue Manual

questions.stem: An IRS employee does not follow an applicable IRM instruction. What does IRC § 7811(a)(3) require?
options: Automatic issuance of a Taxpayer Assistance Order
That the National Taxpayer Advocate construe the TAO factors in the manner most favorable to the taxpayer
Abatement of the tax
Nothing — the IRM is internal
questions.explanation: A rule of construction, not an automatic remedy — which is why the IRM section should be cited by number in a Form 911.
questions.pageTitle: Internal Revenue Manual

questions.stem: Why is the IRM published on irs.gov?
options: As a courtesy
Because FOIA requires administrative staff manuals and instructions to staff affecting the public to be available, electronically since 1996
Because the Code requires it
Because Congress directed it in 2019
questions.explanation: 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(2)(C), with the E-FOIA amendments requiring electronic form.
questions.pageTitle: Internal Revenue Manual

questions.stem: Which FOIA exemption generally supports withholding part of an IRM section?
options: § 552(b)(1), classified national defense material
§ 552(b)(4), trade secrets
§ 552(b)(7)(E), risk of circumvention of the law
§ 552(b)(6), personal privacy
questions.explanation: Such content is marked official use only and redacted, leaving the rest accessible.
questions.pageTitle: Internal Revenue Manual

questions.stem: A representative finds an IRM section on irs.gov dated last year. What should they check before relying on it?
options: Nothing — posted sections are current
Whether interim guidance has changed the procedure since
Whether the section is on the authority list
Whether a Delegation Order supersedes it
questions.explanation: Interim guidance conveys changes where there is insufficient time to update and publish the IRM.
questions.pageTitle: Internal Revenue Manual

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT authority under Reg. § 1.6662-4(d)(3)(iii)?
options: A revenue procedure
A conclusion reached in a leading tax treatise
A private letter ruling issued in 2015
A Joint Committee on Taxation General Explanation
questions.explanation: Treatises, legal periodicals, legal opinions and tax professionals' opinions are expressly excluded, though the authorities they cite may qualify.
questions.pageTitle: Authoritative versus non-authoritative source material

questions.stem: Where does substantial authority sit relative to the other standards?
options: Above more likely than not
Below reasonable basis
Below more likely than not and above reasonable basis
Equivalent to more likely than not
questions.explanation: Reg. § 1.6662-4(d)(2) places it expressly between the two; reasonable basis is the lowest of the three.
questions.pageTitle: Authoritative versus non-authoritative source material

questions.stem: In deciding whether substantial authority exists, what weight is given to the chance the return will not be audited?
options: Substantial weight
Some weight, depending on the item
None — it is not relevant
It is decisive for small items
questions.explanation: Reg. § 1.6662-4(d)(2) excludes it expressly.
questions.pageTitle: Authoritative versus non-authoritative source material

questions.stem: A private letter ruling issued to an unrelated taxpayer in 2015 supports a position. What is its status?
options: Binding precedent
Authority for the substantial authority analysis, but it may not be cited as precedent
Neither authority nor precedent
Authority only for the taxpayer who received it
questions.explanation: It is on the § 1.6662-4 list, and IRC § 6110(k)(3) bars its use as precedent.
questions.pageTitle: Authoritative versus non-authoritative source material

questions.stem: A Tax Court opinion supports the taxpayer's position. A court of appeals in a circuit to which the taxpayer has no right of appeal has held the other way. Is the Tax Court opinion still authority?
options: No — it has been overruled
Yes, unless the Tax Court adopts the court of appeals' holding
Only if the taxpayer discloses on Form 8275
Only for years before the appellate decision
questions.explanation: Reg. § 1.6662-4(d)(3)(iii) states the refinement expressly.
questions.pageTitle: Authoritative versus non-authoritative source material

questions.stem: A treaty article and a later-enacted Code provision conflict. Which governs?
options: The treaty, because treaties are supreme
The Code, because domestic law is supreme
Generally the later in time, because neither has preferential status by reason of what it is
Neither — the conflict is resolved by the competent authority
questions.pageTitle: Tax treaties

questions.stem: What must a taxpayer do who takes the position that a treaty modifies an internal revenue law?
options: Nothing special
Disclose the position on the return or an attached statement under IRC § 6114
File Form 8275-R
Request a private letter ruling
questions.explanation: Failure carries a per-occurrence penalty under IRC § 6712, waivable for reasonable cause and good faith.
questions.pageTitle: Tax treaties

questions.stem: What does a treaty's saving clause do?
options: Preserves the taxpayer's right to elect treaty benefits
Prevents a U.S. citizen or resident from using the treaty to avoid tax on U.S. source income
Saves the treaty from later Code amendments
Extends the treaty to state taxes
questions.explanation: It is why most U.S. clients get no benefit, and its exceptions are the first thing to read.
questions.pageTitle: Tax treaties

questions.stem: Treaty benefits generally run to whom?
options: Citizens of the treaty country
Residents of the treaty country, not necessarily citizens
Anyone with source income in the treaty country
Only corporations
questions.explanation: Establishing residence under the treaty's own definition is the substantive work.
questions.pageTitle: Tax treaties

questions.stem: A nonresident's U.S. source income is exempt under a treaty. Is it exempt from state income tax?
options: Yes, automatically
Yes, if the state has an income tax
Not necessarily — some states do not honor treaty provisions
Only if the treaty names the state
questions.explanation: The IRS says so expressly, and the answer depends on the particular state's law.
questions.pageTitle: Tax treaties

questions.stem: A taxpayer files a 2024 return on March 3, 2025. Absent an extension or exception, the last day for the IRS to assess additional tax is:
options: March 3, 2028
April 15, 2028
March 3, 2031
April 15, 2031
questions.explanation: An early-filed return is deemed filed on the due date; three years from April 15, 2025.
questions.pageTitle: Statute of limitations: assessment, refund, and collection

questions.stem: A taxpayer files a 2021 return on May 1, 2026 with $3,000 of withholding and no other payments. The maximum refund is:
options: It depends on the tax due
questions.explanation: Withholding is deemed paid April 18, 2022, outside the three-year look-back from May 1, 2026.
questions.pageTitle: Statute of limitations: assessment, refund, and collection

questions.stem: Which event does NOT suspend the ten-year collection period?
options: A pending offer in compromise
An accepted installment agreement in good standing
A pending Collection Due Process hearing
The taxpayer's bankruptcy case
questions.explanation: An installment agreement suspends the period only while it is pending or being appealed after rejection, not while it is in effect.
questions.pageTitle: Statute of limitations: assessment, refund, and collection

questions.stem: A math error notice under IRC 6213(b)(1):
options: Is a notice of deficiency
Is not a notice of deficiency, and no Tax Court petition lies on it
Must be preceded by an examination
Starts a 90-day period
questions.pageTitle: Post-filing correspondence (e.g., math error notices, under-reporting notices)

questions.stem: A taxpayer who requests abatement of a math error assessment within 60 days:
options: May have it abated at the Secretary's discretion
Shall have it abated, and any reassessment is then subject to deficiency procedures
Must first pay the tax
Loses the right to contest the item
questions.pageTitle: Post-filing correspondence (e.g., math error notices, under-reporting notices)

questions.stem: Which of the following is *not* within the IRS math error authority?
options: An entry inconsistent with another entry on the return
A correction to reported withholding or estimated tax payments
An omission of information required to substantiate an entry
A credit exceeding a statutory limit expressed as a monetary amount
questions.explanation: It appears nowhere in the § 6213(g)(2) list, and § 6213(b)(1) reaches only cases where tax in excess of that shown is due.
questions.pageTitle: Post-filing correspondence (e.g., math error notices, under-reporting notices)

questions.stem: Which of the following is a "mathematical or clerical error" under IRC 6213(g)(2)?
options: A disputed valuation
A credit claimed in an amount exceeding a statutory limit where the limiting items appear on the return
An unreported item of income found by the IRS
A disagreement about whether an expense is deductible
questions.explanation: Subparagraph (E).
questions.pageTitle: Post-filing correspondence (e.g., math error notices, under-reporting notices)

questions.stem: During the period in which a math error assessment may be abated:
options: The IRS may levy
No levy or court proceeding for collection may be made or begun
Interest stops
The taxpayer must pay the undisputed portion
questions.pageTitle: Post-filing correspondence (e.g., math error notices, under-reporting notices)

questions.stem: A taxpayer mails a refund complaint to a U.S. District Court, postmarked on the last day of the limitation period. It arrives three days later. Is it timely?
options: Yes — timely mailing is timely filing
Yes, if sent by certified mail
No — IRC § 7502 does not apply to any court other than the Tax Court
Yes, if sent by a designated delivery service
questions.explanation: IRC § 7502(d)(1). Only the Tax Court is inside the mailing rule.
questions.pageTitle: Deadlines and timeliness requirements

questions.stem: What effect does sending a document by United States registered mail have?
options: None beyond ordinary mail
Registration is prima facie evidence of delivery and the registration date is deemed the postmark date
It extends the deadline by three days
It is required for all filings
questions.explanation: IRC § 7502(c)(1). Certified mail and electronic filing get similar treatment by regulation.
questions.pageTitle: Deadlines and timeliness requirements

questions.stem: A filing deadline, already extended, falls on a Sunday. When is performance timely?
options: The preceding Friday
The Sunday itself
The next day that is not a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday
The deadline is unaffected by extensions
questions.explanation: IRC § 7503, and the last day is determined including any authorized extension.
questions.pageTitle: Deadlines and timeliness requirements

questions.stem: A practitioner uses a courier service not on the IRS designated list, with tracking showing pickup before the deadline. Delivery is late. Is the filing timely?
options: Yes — the tracking proves timely dispatch
Yes, if the carrier is DHL, FedEx or UPS
No — § 7502 applies only to designated services, and it is the service that is designated, not the carrier
Yes, if the delay was the carrier's fault
questions.explanation: IRC § 7502(f) and the IRS designated list.
questions.pageTitle: Deadlines and timeliness requirements

questions.stem: Whose deadlines are automatically postponed under the mandatory disaster provision?
options: Anyone in the state where the disaster occurred
Only individuals whose principal residence is in the disaster area
A qualified taxpayer, including one whose records necessary to meet the deadline are maintained in the disaster area
Only taxpayers the Secretary specifically identifies
questions.explanation: IRC § 7508A(e)(2) also covers principal place of business, relief workers, individuals visiting who were killed or injured, and a spouse on a joint return.
questions.pageTitle: Deadlines and timeliness requirements

questions.stem: How long does a person entitled to notice have to begin a proceeding to quash a third-party summons?
options: 10 days from notice
20 days from notice
23 days from notice
30 days from service of the summons
questions.explanation: And within the same 20 days a copy of the petition must be mailed by registered or certified mail to the person summoned and the office the notice names.
questions.pageTitle: Third-party correspondence (e.g., witness communications, employment records)

questions.stem: A revenue officer summonses an employer for payroll records to collect an assessment already made against the taxpayer. What rights does the taxpayer have under § 7609?
options: Notice and the right to quash
Notice only
None — a summons in aid of collection of an assessment is excepted
The right to intervene only
questions.explanation: IRC § 7609(c)(2)(D). The taxpayer's protections at that stage lie in the collection appeal routes.
questions.pageTitle: Third-party correspondence (e.g., witness communications, employment records)

questions.stem: A summoned bank never resolves its response. What happens to the assessment period?
options: It runs normally
It is suspended from six months after service until the response is finally resolved
It is suspended only if the taxpayer petitions to quash
It is extended by one year
questions.explanation: IRC § 7609(e)(2) operates regardless of whether the taxpayer acts.
questions.pageTitle: Third-party correspondence (e.g., witness communications, employment records)

questions.stem: Which must a court find before a John Doe summons may be served?
options: Only that the summons relates to a particular person or ascertainable class
That there is probable cause of a crime
That the summons relates to a particular person or class, there is a reasonable basis for believing non-compliance, and the information is not readily available from other sources
That the taxpayer consented
questions.explanation: And since 2019 the information sought must also be narrowly tailored to the identified non-compliance.
questions.pageTitle: Third-party correspondence (e.g., witness communications, employment records)

questions.stem: When must notice of a third-party summons be given?
options: Within 3 days of service and no later than the 23rd day before the examination date
45 days before the contact period
Within 20 days of service
At the same time the summons is served
questions.explanation: The 45-day rule belongs to the § 7602(c) third-party contact notice, which is a different provision.
questions.pageTitle: Third-party correspondence (e.g., witness communications, employment records)

questions.stem: Which is NOT one of the FOIA exemptions as the IRS states them?
options: Classified documents pertaining to national defense and foreign policy
Trade secrets and confidential commercial or financial information
Personal privacy
Investigative information
questions.explanation: The seventh exemption is stated as "law enforcement" — records or information compiled for law enforcement purposes, and only to the extent production would cause one of six specified harms. "Investigative information" is not how the exemption is framed, and the exemption is conditional rather than categorical.
questions.pageTitle: Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests

questions.stem: Part of a requested record is exempt. What must the IRS do?
options: Withhold the entire record
Release the entire record
Release the reasonably segregable portions, indicating the deletions
Release the record only on appeal
questions.explanation: The amount deleted and the exemption relied on are indicated on the released record, and where technically feasible at the place of deletion.
questions.pageTitle: Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests

questions.stem: A representative asks the IRS under FOIA to calculate how an adjustment was derived. What is the IRS obliged to do?
options: Perform the calculation
Nothing — the FOIA applies to existing records and does not require creating one
Refer the request to Appeals
Provide an estimate within 20 days
questions.explanation: The FOIA does not require the IRS to collect, research, analyse, or create a record.
questions.pageTitle: Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests

questions.stem: Under which exemption does IRC § 6103 protect return information from a FOIA request?
options: Exemption 4, trade secrets
Exemption 6, personal privacy
Exemption 3, information exempt under other laws
Exemption 7, law enforcement
questions.explanation: Exemption 3 incorporates statutes that restrict availability, and the IRS names § 6103 as its example.
questions.pageTitle: Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests

questions.stem: The IRS misses the statutory time limits on a properly made request. What follows?
options: The request is deemed granted
The requester is deemed to have exhausted administrative remedies and may sue in Federal District Court
The requester must re-file
Fees are waived
questions.explanation: Reg. § 601.702(c)(9), (10) and (11)(i) are the provisions whose breach produces deemed exhaustion.
questions.pageTitle: Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests

questions.stem: Which of the following is tax evasion rather than tax avoidance?
options: Deducting mortgage interest on a qualified residence
Contributing to a retirement plan to reduce current income
