Claiming a credit the taxpayer qualifies for
Omitting cash receipts from a business from the return
questions.explanation: The first three are the Code operating as written; omitting known income is willful understatement.
questions.pageTitle: Tax avoidance vs. tax evasion

questions.stem: A taxpayer willfully fails to file for three years but takes no steps to conceal anything. Which section fits?
options: IRC § 7201, felony evasion
IRC § 7203, misdemeanor failure to file
questions.explanation: Section 7201 requires a willful attempt — an affirmative act — beyond the omission itself.
questions.pageTitle: Tax avoidance vs. tax evasion

questions.stem: A preparer knowingly inserts fabricated deductions supplied by a client who is unaware they are fabricated. Is the preparer exposed under IRC § 7206(2)?
options: No — the taxpayer must be complicit
No — only the signer is liable
Yes — it applies whether or not the falsity is with the taxpayer's knowledge or consent
Only if the tax understated exceeds $5,000
questions.explanation: The statute says so in terms, and the offence is a felony.
questions.pageTitle: Tax avoidance vs. tax evasion

questions.stem: The IRS establishes that part of an underpayment is due to fraud. How much is subject to the IRC § 6663 penalty?
options: Only the portion proved fraudulent
The entire underpayment, unless the taxpayer shows by a preponderance which portion is not attributable to fraud
Half the underpayment
None, absent a criminal conviction
questions.explanation: IRC § 6663(b) reverses the default once any portion is established.
questions.pageTitle: Tax avoidance vs. tax evasion

questions.stem: A taxpayer whose returns are all accurate conceals assets from a revenue officer to defeat collection. What is the exposure?
options: None — the returns were correct
A civil penalty only
IRC § 7201, which reaches evasion of the payment of tax as well as its assessment
IRC § 7203 only
questions.explanation: Concealment aimed at defeating payment is the affirmative act, and IRC § 7212(a) may also be in play.
questions.pageTitle: Tax avoidance vs. tax evasion

questions.stem: Form 8275 may be used to avoid the portion of the accuracy-related penalty attributable to which of the following?
options: A substantial understatement for a non-tax-shelter item where the position has a reasonable basis
Negligence
Disregard of regulations
A substantial understatement on a tax shelter item
questions.explanation: Disregard of regulations is Form 8275-R's territory; negligence and tax shelter understatements cannot be cured by disclosure on either form.
questions.pageTitle: Tax return disclosure statements

questions.stem: A taxpayer takes a position contrary to a Treasury regulation. What is required to avoid the disregard-of-regulations penalty?
options: Filing Form 8275
Filing Form 8275-R only
Filing Form 8275-R and a position representing a good-faith challenge to the validity of the regulation
Substantial authority alone
questions.explanation: Reg. § 1.6662-3(c)(1) adds the good-faith-challenge requirement on top of disclosure.
questions.pageTitle: Tax return disclosure statements

questions.stem: Which best describes the reasonable basis standard?
options: Any position that is not frivolous
A relatively high standard, significantly higher than not frivolous, not met by a merely arguable position
The same as substantial authority
More likely than not
questions.explanation: It sits below substantial authority and well above not frivolous.
questions.pageTitle: Tax return disclosure statements

questions.stem: A taxpayer's records are incomplete and the items are unsubstantiated. Does a Form 8275 disclosure avoid the accuracy-related penalty?
options: Yes, if the disclosure is detailed
Yes, for the disclosed items only
No — disclosure cannot cure a failure to keep proper books and records or to substantiate
Yes, if filed with the original return
questions.explanation: The instructions say so directly.
questions.pageTitle: Tax return disclosure statements

questions.stem: For a tax shelter item in a tax year ending after 22 October 2004, what is the only exception to the substantial understatement portion of the penalty?
options: Adequate disclosure with a reasonable basis
Substantial authority
Reasonable cause
Filing Form 8275-R
questions.explanation: Disclosure and substantial authority both drop out for tax shelter items.
questions.pageTitle: Tax return disclosure statements

questions.stem: Which is a statutory element of "significant hardship" under IRC § 7811(a)(2)?
options: Disagreement with a proposed adjustment
A delay of more than 30 days in resolving taxpayer account problems
Inability to afford the tax
A pending Appeals conference
questions.explanation: The others are an immediate threat of adverse action, significant costs including representation fees, and irreparable injury or long-term adverse impact.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer Advocate Service (e.g., criteria for requesting assistance)

questions.stem: Who may rescind a Taxpayer Assistance Order?
options: The revenue officer's group manager
Any IRS territory manager
Only the National Taxpayer Advocate, the Commissioner, or the Deputy Commissioner, with a written explanation
Only a court
questions.explanation: IRC § 7811(c) names all three and requires the written explanation to go to the National Taxpayer Advocate.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer Advocate Service (e.g., criteria for requesting assistance)

questions.stem: An IRS employee has not followed an IRM provision. What does IRC § 7811(a)(3) require?
options: Automatic issuance of a Taxpayer Assistance Order
That the factors be construed in the manner most favorable to the taxpayer
Referral to the Treasury Inspector General
Abatement of the tax
questions.explanation: It is a rule of construction, not an automatic remedy, and it is why the IRM citation belongs in the Form 911.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer Advocate Service (e.g., criteria for requesting assistance)

questions.stem: Which best describes the role of the Taxpayer Advocate Service?
options: A second level of appeal after the Independent Office of Appeals
An independent office within the IRS that helps taxpayers resolve problems the system has not resolved
A body outside the IRS that reviews determinations
The office that issues notices of deficiency
questions.explanation: It is inside the IRS but independent, and it is not an appeal of a determination.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer Advocate Service (e.g., criteria for requesting assistance)

questions.stem: What happens to a limitation period when a taxpayer applies for a Taxpayer Assistance Order?
options: Nothing
It is suspended from the application date to the Advocate's decision, plus any period specified in the order
It is extended by one year
It restarts
questions.explanation: IRC § 7811(d), and it applies to the actions described in § 7811(b).
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer Advocate Service (e.g., criteria for requesting assistance)

questions.stem: How long is an IP PIN valid?
options: For the taxpayer's lifetime
One calendar year, with a new one issued annually
Three years
Until the taxpayer opts out
questions.explanation: A new IP PIN is generated each year for the account; there is no fixed number of years after which issuance stops.
questions.pageTitle: Identity Theft

questions.stem: Which is NOT a recommended step for someone who suspects tax-related identity theft?
options: Responding to any IRS notice received
Reporting the theft and following the recovery steps at IdentityTheft.gov
Holding off on filing and paying until the matter is resolved
Obtaining an IP PIN
questions.explanation: The IRS lists "file returns and pay tax as usual" among the steps; suspending compliance adds penalties the theft does not excuse.
questions.pageTitle: Identity Theft

questions.stem: A taxpayer who opted into the IP PIN programme online has not received a letter with this year's number. What should the representative do?
options: File Form 15227 for a replacement
Have the taxpayer retrieve the IP PIN from the IRS online account
File without an IP PIN
Wait for the CP01A Notice
questions.explanation: No CP01A is mailed to voluntary opt-ins, and the IRS says expressly not to use Form 15227 to apply for a new IP PIN.
questions.pageTitle: Identity Theft

questions.stem: A client with a valid IP PIN finds her dependent has already been claimed on another return for 2025. Can she e-file?
options: No — she must paper-file with supporting documents
Yes, because the primary taxpayer's return includes a valid IP PIN
Only if the dependent also has an IP PIN
Only after the IRS resolves the duplicate claim
questions.explanation: From 2024 returns onward, and the dependent needs an IP PIN only if one was previously issued.
questions.pageTitle: Identity Theft

questions.stem: Can the IRS tell a taxpayer who wrongly claimed their dependent?
options: Yes, on written request
Yes, after the duplicate claim is resolved
No — disclosure is limited to the return's primary and secondary taxpayers
Yes, if a police report is filed
questions.explanation: IRC § 6103 governs, and the IRS states the limit expressly.
questions.pageTitle: Identity Theft

questions.stem: Which of the following is not required to pass the Tax Court's examination to be admitted to practise before it?
options: An enrolled agent
A CPA
A licensed attorney
None of them — all must pass it
questions.explanation: Rule 200(a)(2) admits an attorney on a current certificate of good standing; Rule 200(a)(3) requires the Court's written examination of every non-attorney applicant, whatever their other credentials.
questions.pageTitle: Judicial levels of representation beyond the scope of EA representation

questions.stem: What does an enrolled agent's Circular 230 enrolment authorise?
options: Practice before the IRS and the U.S. Tax Court
Practice before the IRS only
Practice before any federal court in tax matters
Practice before the IRS and the U.S. District Courts
questions.explanation: Circular 230 is made under authority to regulate practice before the Department of the Treasury.
questions.pageTitle: Judicial levels of representation beyond the scope of EA representation

questions.stem: A corporation receives a notice of deficiency and does not want to retain counsel. Who may represent it in the Tax Court?
options: No one — counsel is required
Its enrolled agent
An authorized officer of the corporation
Any employee
questions.explanation: Rule 24(b)(1)(B). The officer appears as the corporation, not as a representative.
questions.pageTitle: Judicial levels of representation beyond the scope of EA representation

questions.stem: After a decision in a small tax case, who may appeal?
options: Both the taxpayer and the IRS
Only the IRS
Only the taxpayer
Neither — the decision is not reviewable in any other court
questions.explanation: IRC § 7463(b), which also provides that such a decision is not treated as precedent.
questions.pageTitle: Judicial levels of representation beyond the scope of EA representation

questions.stem: An unadmitted practitioner files an entry of appearance in the Tax Court. What is the effect?
options: It is effective on filing
It is not effective until the practitioner is admitted
It is effective for 90 days
It is effective if the taxpayer consents
questions.explanation: Rule 24(a)(3), though the Court may recognise counsel who can and will be promptly admitted.
questions.pageTitle: Judicial levels of representation beyond the scope of EA representation

questions.sectionTitle: Representing a taxpayer in the collection process
questions.stem: The maximum extension of time to pay tax shown on a return is generally:
options: 30 days
6 months from the date fixed for payment, longer if the taxpayer is abroad
18 months
10 years
questions.pageTitle: Extension of time to pay (e.g., Form 1127)

questions.sectionTitle: Representing a taxpayer in the collection process
questions.stem: "Undue hardship" for these purposes means:
options: Any inconvenience in raising the money
Substantial financial loss, such as a sale of property at a sacrifice price
Inability to pay in a single instalment
A general statement of financial difficulty
questions.explanation: Reg. § 1.6161-1(b), which also says a general statement will not do.
questions.pageTitle: Extension of time to pay (e.g., Form 1127)

questions.sectionTitle: Representing a taxpayer in the collection process
questions.stem: While an extension of time to pay is in force:
options: Interest stops running
Interest continues to run, and payment is due at expiry without notice and demand
The collection statute is suspended
Penalties and interest are both abated
questions.pageTitle: Extension of time to pay (e.g., Form 1127)

questions.sectionTitle: Representing a taxpayer in the collection process
questions.stem: An executor needs more time to pay estate tax under IRC 6161. The application is made on:
options: Form 1127
Form 4768, Part III
Form 9465
Form 843
questions.explanation: Section 6161 authorises the extension; Form 1127 is for tax shown on a return and for deficiencies.
questions.pageTitle: Extension of time to pay (e.g., Form 1127)

questions.sectionTitle: Representing a taxpayer in the collection process
questions.stem: Form 1127 must be accompanied by:
options: A statement of hardship alone
Evidence of the hardship, a statement of assets and liabilities, and itemised receipts and disbursements for each of the 3 preceding months
The prior year's return
A bond in every case
questions.pageTitle: Extension of time to pay (e.g., Form 1127)

questions.sectionTitle: Representing a taxpayer in the collection process
questions.stem: While an accepted installment agreement is in effect and being paid on time, the ten-year collection period:
options: Is suspended for the life of the agreement
Continues to run
Is extended by 30 days per year
Restarts
questions.explanation: Section 6331(k)(3)(B) carves the in-effect period out of the suspension rule.
questions.pageTitle: Installment agreements: simple payment plans and the CSED

questions.sectionTitle: Representing a taxpayer in the collection process
questions.stem: Under the current IRM, the constraint on a simple payment plan's monthly amount is:
options: A 72-month maximum term
Full payment of all balances, including accrued penalties and interest, by the CSED
A minimum of 10 percent of the balance annually
The taxpayer's disposable income on Form 433-A
questions.explanation: The 72-month rule was removed when the subsection was rewritten.
questions.pageTitle: Installment agreements: simple payment plans and the CSED

questions.sectionTitle: Representing a taxpayer in the collection process
questions.stem: Which combination produces the lowest setup fee for a long-term plan, ignoring low-income status?
options: Apply by phone, pay by cheque
Apply online, pay by cheque
Apply by phone, pay by direct debit
Apply online, pay by direct debit
questions.explanation: The online and direct debit reductions compound.
questions.pageTitle: Installment agreements: simple payment plans and the CSED

questions.sectionTitle: Representing a taxpayer in the collection process
questions.stem: A taxpayer's assessed balance is $52,000, with a further $3,000 of accrued but unassessed interest. For the simple payment plan ceiling, the relevant amount is:
options: $55,000, so he does not qualify
$52,000, so he does not qualify without paying it down
Whatever remains after the CSED calculation
questions.explanation: The ceiling counts the unpaid balance of assessment and excludes accrued unassessed amounts — and $52,000 is over it.
questions.pageTitle: Installment agreements: simple payment plans and the CSED
