options: From the extended payment date
From the original unextended due date
From the date of notice and demand
No interest is due
questions.explanation: IRC § 6601(b)(1) determines the last date prescribed for payment without regard to any extension of time for payment or any § 6159 installment agreement.
questions.pageTitle: Interest recalculation

questions.stem: What is the underpayment rate under IRC § 6621(a)(2)?
options: The federal short-term rate
The federal short-term rate plus 2 percentage points
The federal short-term rate plus 3 percentage points
The federal short-term rate plus 5 percentage points
questions.explanation: Five points applies only to a large corporate underpayment under § 6621(c)(1); two points is the corporate overpayment rate.
questions.pageTitle: Interest recalculation

questions.stem: Notice and demand is made for an amount exactly equal to the § 6601(e)(3) threshold. What payment window avoids interest for the period after the notice?
options: 21 calendar days
10 business days
30 days
10 calendar days
questions.explanation: The statute applies the shorter window where the amount "equals or exceeds" the threshold, and measures it in business days.
questions.pageTitle: Interest recalculation

questions.stem: A net operating loss carried back eliminates an earlier year's tax entirely. What happens to the interest already accrued on that year?
options: It is eliminated with the tax
It is recomputed from the original due date
It is preserved for the period ending with the filing date for the year the loss arose
It is abated under § 6404(e)
questions.explanation: IRC § 6601(d)(1). The taxpayer had the use of the money in the interim.
questions.pageTitle: Interest recalculation

questions.stem: How often is the interest rate redetermined?
options: Annually
Quarterly, from the federal short-term rate for the first month of each calendar quarter
Monthly
Whenever the IRS issues a revenue ruling
questions.explanation: IRC § 6621(b) — and the rate so determined applies during the first calendar quarter beginning after that month, so a multi-year balance accrues at a series of rates.
questions.pageTitle: Interest recalculation

questions.stem: Which may not be requested on Form 843?
options: Abatement of the § 6672 trust fund recovery penalty
Abatement of income tax
Abatement of interest under § 6404(e)(1)
Refund of the § 6715 dyed-fuel penalty
questions.explanation: The instructions bar abatement of income, estate or gift tax — reflecting IRC § 6404(b). The other three are on the form's own list.
questions.pageTitle: Procedures for requesting abatement

questions.stem: An employee had social security tax withheld in error. When may the employee file Form 843?
options: At any time within the claim period
Only if the employer will not adjust the overcollection
Only if the employer files first
Never; only the employer may claim it
questions.explanation: And note the mirror image — an employer may not use Form 843 for FICA, RRTA or withheld income tax at all.
questions.pageTitle: Procedures for requesting abatement

questions.stem: A single IRS delay in one ministerial act caused interest to accrue across three tax years. How many Forms 843 are required?
options: One for each year
One, with the applicable boxes checked on line 4
One for each type of tax
None; interest claims use Form 1040-X
questions.explanation: This is one of the two exceptions to the one-form-per-period rule, the other being a net-interest-rate-of-zero request.
questions.pageTitle: Procedures for requesting abatement

questions.stem: What must a representative attach when filing Form 843 for a client?
options: A signed engagement letter
The original or a copy of Form 2848 authorising the representative for the request
A Form 8821
Nothing, if a power of attorney is already on the CAF
questions.explanation: The instructions require it attached to the Form 843, not merely on file.
questions.pageTitle: Procedures for requesting abatement

questions.stem: The instructions ask a § 6404(e)(1) claimant to explain why failure to abate would be "grossly unfair treatment." What is that requirement's status?
options: A statutory element of § 6404(e)
A requirement of Reg. § 301.6404-2
A narrative requirement of the instructions only — the statutory test is unreasonable error or delay in a ministerial or managerial act
The § 6404(h) standard of review
questions.explanation: The phrase appears in neither the statute nor the regulation. Section 6404(h) review is for abuse of discretion.
questions.pageTitle: Procedures for requesting abatement

questions.stem: How many inspections of a taxpayer's books of account may the IRS make for one taxable year?
options: As many as necessary
One, unless the taxpayer requests otherwise or the Secretary notifies the taxpayer in writing after investigation that another is necessary
Two
One, with no exceptions
questions.explanation: IRC § 7605(b). An oral statement that another look is needed does not satisfy the written-notice exception.
questions.pageTitle: IRS authority to investigate

questions.stem: When must a third-party contact notice be provided?
options: At the same time as the first contact
At least 30 days before the contact
At least 45 days before the beginning of the specified period
Within one year of the contact
questions.explanation: IRC § 7602(c)(1)(B), and the period specified may not exceed one year — though successive notices may aggregate to more.
questions.pageTitle: IRS authority to investigate

questions.stem: A case is recommended to the Attorney General for criminal prosecution. What happens to the summons power?
options: It continues with supervisory approval
It is limited to the taxpayer
No summons may be issued and no § 7604 enforcement action begun with respect to that person
It continues for civil purposes only
questions.explanation: IRC § 7602(d)(1). A § 6103(h)(3)(B) disclosure request is the other trigger.
questions.pageTitle: IRS authority to investigate

questions.stem: A summons under IRC § 7602(a)(2) is issued on 1 June. What is the earliest date it may fix for appearance?
options: 6 June
11 June
16 June
Any date the Secretary considers reasonable
questions.explanation: IRC § 7605(a) requires the date fixed to be not less than 10 days from the date of the summons.
questions.pageTitle: IRS authority to investigate

questions.stem: When may the IRS use financial status or economic reality examination techniques to determine the existence of unreported income?
options: At any time during an examination
Only with the taxpayer's consent
Only where there is a reasonable indication of a likelihood of unreported income
Only in a criminal investigation
questions.explanation: IRC § 7602(e), added by the IRS Restructuring and Reform Act of 1998.
questions.pageTitle: IRS authority to investigate

questions.stem: Before which of the following may the § 7525 privilege be asserted?
options: The IRS only
The IRS and state taxing agencies
All Federal agencies
State taxing agencies only
questions.explanation: Of the choices offered, only the IRS. The statute also reaches a noncriminal tax proceeding in Federal court brought by or against the United States, but it does not extend to state taxing agencies or to Federal agencies generally.
questions.pageTitle: Limited practitioner privilege (e.g., IRC Section 7525)

questions.stem: An enrolled agent's client becomes the subject of an IRS criminal investigation. What protection does § 7525 give the earlier written advice?
options: Full protection, because the advice was given while the matter was civil
None — the privilege may only be asserted in noncriminal matters
Protection unless the IRS shows fraud
Protection only in Federal court
questions.explanation: Both forums in IRC § 7525(a)(2) are limited to noncriminal matters.
questions.pageTitle: Limited practitioner privilege (e.g., IRC Section 7525)

questions.stem: Which best describes what § 7525 protects?
options: A new statutory privilege for all practitioner communications
Any communication between a practitioner and a client
Tax advice, to the extent it would be privileged if the practitioner were an attorney
All working papers created during an engagement
questions.explanation: The statute borrows the common-law attorney-client privilege and applies it "to the extent the communication would be considered a privileged communication if it were between a taxpayer and an attorney."
questions.pageTitle: Limited practitioner privilege (e.g., IRC Section 7525)

questions.stem: A practitioner writes a memorandum used to market a partnership whose significant purpose is Federal income tax avoidance. Is the memorandum privileged under § 7525?
options: Yes, if the analysis was given in good faith
Yes, unless the IRS proves a significant purpose of avoidance
No — the tax-shelter exception removes the privilege
Yes, because the client is a partnership rather than a corporation
questions.explanation: IRC § 7525(b) removes the privilege from written communications in connection with the promotion of participation in a tax shelter, and since 2004 it reaches any person, not only corporations.
questions.pageTitle: Limited practitioner privilege (e.g., IRC Section 7525)

questions.stem: Who is a "federally authorized tax practitioner"?
options: Any return preparer with a PTIN
Attorneys and CPAs only
Anyone authorised under Federal law to practise before the IRS where that practice is subject to 31 U.S.C. § 330
Enrolled agents only
questions.explanation: That is the definition in IRC § 7525(a)(3)(A) — the statute behind Circular 230.
questions.pageTitle: Limited practitioner privilege (e.g., IRC Section 7525)

questions.stem: How long must records supporting the basis of a rental property be kept?
options: Three years from the return's due date
Six years
So long as their contents may become material in the administration of any internal revenue law
Until the property is placed in service
questions.explanation: Reg. § 1.6001-1(e). Basis records stay material until the year of disposition closes.
questions.pageTitle: Verification and substantiation of entries on the return

questions.stem: Which is no longer one of the categories subject to the IRC § 274(d) substantiation rules?
options: Travel expenses
Gifts
Entertainment
Listed property
questions.explanation: TCJA repealed the entertainment deduction for amounts paid or incurred after 31 December 2017, and the current § 274(d) list is travel, gifts and listed property.
questions.pageTitle: Verification and substantiation of entries on the return

questions.stem: A taxpayer substantiates the amount, date and location of a business meal but cannot show who attended or why. What is the result?
options: A reasonable portion is allowed
The item is disallowed — the elements are conjunctive
The examiner must accept the taxpayer's statement
The item is allowed if the amount is small
questions.explanation: Business purpose and business relationship are separate elements, and § 274(d) allows no deduction unless each is substantiated.
questions.pageTitle: Verification and substantiation of entries on the return

questions.stem: What does "sufficient evidence corroborating the taxpayer's own statement" permit?
options: The taxpayer's testimony alone
An estimate, if reasonable
The taxpayer's statement supported by corroborating evidence
Nothing — only adequate records will do
questions.explanation: It is a genuine alternative to adequate records, but it requires corroboration; the statement standing alone is not enough.
questions.pageTitle: Verification and substantiation of entries on the return

questions.stem: In what setting does IRC § 6201(d) place a production requirement on the Secretary?
options: At the examination, on request
In Appeals
In any court proceeding, where the taxpayer asserts a reasonable dispute and has fully cooperated
At any stage, without condition
questions.explanation: Both conditions must be met, and the provision operates by its terms "in any court proceeding."
questions.pageTitle: Verification and substantiation of entries on the return

questions.stem: Where does a field examination generally take place?
options: At the closest IRS office
Where the taxpayer's original books, records and source documents are maintained
At the representative's office
At the address shown on the return, in all cases
questions.explanation: Usually the principal place of business, in the case of a sole proprietorship or entity.
questions.pageTitle: IRS authority to fix time and place of investigation

questions.stem: A sole proprietor represents in writing that a field examination at her shop would essentially require it to close. Where will the Service move it?
options: To the taxpayer's home
To the representative's office
To a Service office in the district where the records are maintained
Nowhere — the request is not a recognised ground
questions.explanation: On verification of the written representation, the examination moves to a Service office.
questions.pageTitle: IRS authority to fix time and place of investigation

questions.stem: An enrolled agent asks that an examination be scheduled outside filing season. What does the regulation say?
options: The Service must accommodate the representative's filing-season workload
The Service may schedule throughout the year without regard to seasonal fluctuations of taxpayers or their representatives
Scheduling in filing season is unreasonable per se
The Service must schedule outside normal business hours on request
questions.explanation: The Service will try to minimise adverse effects, but seasonality is not a constraint on reasonableness.
questions.pageTitle: IRS authority to fix time and place of investigation

questions.stem: A taxpayer requests a transfer of the place of examination. An assessment period will expire in eleven months. What may the Service require?
options: Nothing further
Payment of the proposed deficiency
A written agreement to extend the limitations period for up to one year
Withdrawal of the Form 2848
questions.explanation: Where a limitations period will expire within thirteen months of the request, the Service may condition an otherwise permissible transfer on a written extension.
questions.pageTitle: IRS authority to fix time and place of investigation

questions.stem: May the IRS inspect a taxpayer's books of account for the same year twice?
options: Never
Only with a court order
Yes, if the taxpayer requests it or the Service gives written notice after investigation that an additional inspection is necessary
Yes, without restriction
questions.explanation: Those are the two exceptions in IRC § 7605(b).
questions.pageTitle: IRS authority to fix time and place of investigation

questions.stem: How does the IRS first notify a taxpayer that a return has been selected for audit?
options: By telephone
By mail
By email
By a visit from a revenue agent
questions.explanation: The IRS states that it will notify by mail and that it won't initiate an audit by telephone.
questions.pageTitle: Steps in the process

questions.stem: Where is a field audit conducted?
options: At an IRS office
By mail
At the taxpayer's home, place of business, or accountant's or representative's office
At the Independent Office of Appeals
questions.explanation: An in-person interview at an IRS office is an office audit; by mail is a correspondence audit.
questions.pageTitle: Steps in the process

questions.stem: Which describes a "no change" conclusion?
options: The IRS proposed changes but withdrew them
The taxpayer substantiated all of the items being reviewed
The taxpayer agreed with the proposed changes
The audit was closed for lack of response
questions.explanation: "Agreed" and "disagreed" both begin with proposed changes the taxpayer understands.
questions.pageTitle: Steps in the process

questions.stem: A taxpayer under a mail audit has already used the automatic extension, and a notice of deficiency has now issued. What further time is available?
options: A second automatic 30 days
30 days on the manager's approval
None for documents, and the 90-day Tax Court petition period cannot be extended
90 additional days
questions.explanation: The extension is one-time and automatic; once the notice of deficiency issues, no additional time for supporting documentation is available.
questions.pageTitle: Steps in the process

questions.stem: Which condition attaches to filing an appeal after a disagreed examination, but not to a manager conference or mediation?
options: Payment of the proposed deficiency
Enough time remaining on the statute of limitations
A signed examination report
A Form 2848 on file
questions.explanation: The IRS names the three routes and attaches the statute-of-limitations condition to the appeal.
questions.pageTitle: Steps in the process

questions.stem: A taxpayer does not respond to a 30-day letter. What happens next?
options: The tax is assessed immediately
The case closes as agreed
The IRS issues a notice of deficiency, starting the Tax Court petition period
The case goes to Appeals automatically
questions.explanation: The 90-day letter follows, and only after the petition period lapses without a petition does a bill issue.
questions.pageTitle: Interpretation and analysis of Revenue Agent Report (RAR) (e.g., 30-day letter)

questions.stem: An examination report proposes changes of $18,000 for 2023 and $40,000 for 2024. What must the taxpayer file to appeal both years?
options: Form 12203 for 2023 and a formal protest for 2024
A formal written protest for both years
A small case request for both years
Form 9423
questions.explanation: Exceeding the threshold in any tax period requires a formal written protest for all periods involved.
questions.pageTitle: Interpretation and analysis of Revenue Agent Report (RAR) (e.g., 30-day letter)

questions.stem: Where should a formal written protest be sent?
options: To the Independent Office of Appeals
To the IRS address shown on the letter explaining the appeal rights
To the Taxpayer Advocate Service
To the U.S. Tax Court
questions.explanation: Sending it directly to Appeals delays the case and may prevent Appeals from considering it.
questions.pageTitle: Interpretation and analysis of Revenue Agent Report (RAR) (e.g., 30-day letter)

questions.stem: An enrolled agent files a protest based entirely on the client's records and statements. Which perjury statement applies?
options: The taxpayer's own statement
The representative's personal-knowledge statement
The representative's no-personal-knowledge statement
None — a representative does not sign under penalties of perjury
questions.explanation: Pub. 5 gives two representative statements, and facts known only from the client are not the representative's personal knowledge.
questions.pageTitle: Interpretation and analysis of Revenue Agent Report (RAR) (e.g., 30-day letter)

questions.stem: A 30-day letter arrives with seven months left on the assessment period. What is the practical consequence?
options: None — the protest tolls the statute
Appeals generally will not take the case without sufficient statute remaining, so the choice is a consent or a notice of deficiency
The IRS must abate the proposed tax
The taxpayer gets an automatic extension of the ASED
questions.explanation: Filing a protest does not create the time Appeals needs; the client must decide between extending and litigating.
questions.pageTitle: Interpretation and analysis of Revenue Agent Report (RAR) (e.g., 30-day letter)

questions.stem: A CP2000 notice:
options: Assesses additional tax
Proposes changes arising from an information return mismatch and is not a bill
Is a notice of deficiency
Starts the 90-day Tax Court period
questions.pageTitle: Interpretation and analysis of CP-2000 notice and correspondence audits

questions.stem: A taxpayer agrees with a CP2000 and has no other income, credits or expenses to report. He must:
options: File Form 1040-X
Sign and return the response form; no amended return is needed
File Form 843
Petition the Tax Court
questions.pageTitle: Interpretation and analysis of CP-2000 notice and correspondence audits

questions.stem: A taxpayer agrees with a CP2000 but has additional deductions the notice did not consider. She should:
options: Do nothing further
File Form 1040-X marked "CP2000" and submit it with the response form
Wait for the notice of deficiency
File Form 2848
questions.pageTitle: Interpretation and analysis of CP-2000 notice and correspondence audits

questions.stem: A notice of deficiency is mailed to a taxpayer in the United States on 1 March. The last day to petition the Tax Court is:
options: 31 March
90 days after 1 March, not counting a Saturday, Sunday or DC legal holiday as the last day
150 days after 1 March
Three years after the return was filed
questions.pageTitle: Interpretation and analysis of CP-2000 notice and correspondence audits

questions.stem: While the period for petitioning the Tax Court runs, the IRS:
options: May assess and levy
May not assess the deficiency or begin levy or court collection proceedings
May levy but not assess
May assess but not levy
questions.pageTitle: Interpretation and analysis of CP-2000 notice and correspondence audits

questions.stem: A taxpayer cannot pay a proposed deficiency and wants judicial review. Which forum is available?
options: U.S. District Court
U.S. Court of Federal Claims
U.S. Tax Court
Any of the three
questions.explanation: The Tax Court is generally a prepayment forum; the other two are refund forums requiring full payment and a timely claim.
questions.pageTitle: Explanations of taxpayer options (e.g. agree or appeal)

questions.stem: Settlement talks with Appeals are progressing well as the Tax Court petition period runs out. What should the representative do?
options: Request an extension from Appeals
Request an extension from the Tax Court
File the petition to preserve the forum and continue negotiating
Rely on the discussions to toll the period
questions.explanation: The period is set by law and neither the IRS nor the court can change it; it runs even while discussions continue.
questions.pageTitle: Explanations of taxpayer options (e.g. agree or appeal)

questions.stem: A refund claim is disallowed by notice. Appeals considers it for eighteen months and sustains the disallowance. How long does the taxpayer have to sue?
options: Two years from the Appeals decision
Two years from the notice of claim disallowance, unextended by Appeals' consideration
Six months from the Appeals decision
Ninety days from the Appeals decision
questions.explanation: Appeals' consideration does not extend the period, though mutual agreement may.
questions.pageTitle: Explanations of taxpayer options (e.g. agree or appeal)

questions.stem: Who may represent a taxpayer at an Appeals conference?
options: Anyone the taxpayer designates
An attorney, CPA or enrolled agent
Only an attorney
Only the taxpayer, in person
questions.explanation: A person who does not qualify may be included as a witness but may not represent.
questions.pageTitle: Explanations of taxpayer options (e.g. agree or appeal)

questions.stem: A taxpayer elects the small tax case procedure in the Tax Court. What is given up?
options: The right to be represented
Review in any other court, and any precedential value of the decision
The right to settle with Appeals
Nothing
questions.explanation: IRC § 7463(b). New material raised for the first time at an Appeals conference, by contrast, generally sends the case back to the originating office.
questions.pageTitle: Explanations of taxpayer options (e.g. agree or appeal)

questions.stem: At what stage does IRC § 7491 shift the burden of proof?
options: At the start of the examination
When the 30-day letter issues
In a court proceeding, on conditions
At the Appeals conference
questions.explanation: The statute says "in any court proceeding," and the shift depends on the § 7491(a)(2) conditions being met.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer's burden of proof

questions.stem: Which is NOT a condition of the § 7491(a) shift?
options: The taxpayer complied with the Code's substantiation requirements
The taxpayer maintained all required records and cooperated with reasonable requests
The taxpayer paid the proposed deficiency
An entity taxpayer meets the net worth and employee limits
questions.explanation: Payment is not a condition; the three conditions are substantiation, records-and-cooperation, and for entities the § 7430(c)(4)(A)(ii) limits.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer's burden of proof

questions.stem: What does IRC § 7491(c) place on the Secretary?
options: The burden of proof on all penalties against any taxpayer
The burden of production on penalties against an individual, in a court proceeding
The burden of disproving reasonable cause
Nothing — penalties are always the taxpayer's to disprove
questions.explanation: Production, individuals, court proceeding — and reasonable cause remains the taxpayer's affirmative case.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer's burden of proof

questions.stem: In a Tax Court case involving fraud with intent to evade tax, who bears the burden and to what standard?
options: The petitioner, by a preponderance
The respondent, by a preponderance
The respondent, by clear and convincing evidence
The petitioner, by clear and convincing evidence
questions.explanation: IRC § 7454(a) and Tax Court Rule 142(b).
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer's burden of proof

questions.stem: In a transferee liability case, what must the Commissioner prove?
options: Both that the petitioner is liable as a transferee and that the transferor owed the tax
That the petitioner is liable as a transferee, but not that the transferor was liable for the tax
Neither — the petitioner bears the whole burden
Only the amount of the transfer
questions.explanation: IRC § 6902(a) splits it expressly.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer's burden of proof

questions.stem: In which situation is the appeals process available?
options: The taxpayer received a bill that made no mention of appeal rights
The taxpayer disagrees with an IRS decision communicated in a letter explaining the right to
The taxpayer agrees with the adjustment but cannot pay it
The taxpayer failed to provide information the examiner requested and now wants to supply it
questions.explanation: Appeals resolves disagreement with a determination; affordability and a bare bill are not grounds.
questions.pageTitle: Right to appeal

questions.stem: Which is not one of the rights enumerated in the Taxpayer Bill of Rights?
options: The right to be informed
The right to pay no more than the correct amount of tax
The right to a replacement examination
The right to appeal a decision of the IRS in an independent forum
questions.explanation: The ten enumerated rights do not include any right to have an examination redone.
questions.pageTitle: Right to appeal

questions.stem: What did the Taxpayer First Act of 2019 change about Appeals?
options: It abolished the appeals function and replaced it with mediation
It established the Independent Office of Appeals in the Code and made the resolution process
It moved Appeals under the Office of Chief Counsel
It limited appeals to collection matters
questions.explanation: Before 2019 Appeals existed by administrative arrangement; the Act put it in the statute.
questions.pageTitle: Right to appeal

questions.stem: A taxpayer who received a notice of deficiency requests referral to Appeals and is refused. What is the taxpayer entitled to?
options: Nothing; referral is discretionary
An automatic referral on a second request
A written notice giving a detailed description of the facts, the basis for the denial, how that
Immediate issuance of a second notice of deficiency
questions.explanation: unless the denial rests on the issue being a frivolous position, in which case those requirements do not apply.
questions.pageTitle: Right to appeal

questions.stem: Which statement about the independence of Appeals is correct?
options: Appeals personnel report to the examination function that developed the case
Chief Counsel staff who prepared the case for litigation ordinarily advise Appeals on it
All Appeals personnel report to the Chief of Appeals, who reports directly to the Commissioner
Appeals decisions are reviewed by the examining agent before issuance
questions.explanation: The statute also directs that legal advice to Appeals come, so far as practicable, from Chief Counsel staff not involved in the case or in preparing it for litigation.
questions.pageTitle: Right to appeal

questions.stem: In which circumstance may a taxpayer avoid filing a formal written protest?
options: The taxpayer has income below a stated amount
The taxpayer qualifies for the small case request procedure
The taxpayer agrees not to take the case to the Tax Court
The taxpayer is represented by a practitioner holding a power of attorney
questions.explanation: A formal protest is required in all cases unless a small case request or another special appeal procedure applies.
questions.pageTitle: Request for Appeals consideration

questions.stem: A proposed adjustment covers three years. Two are well below the small case threshold and one is above it. What is required?
options: A small case request for the two low years and a formal protest for the third
A formal written protest for all three years
A small case request for all three years
Separate appeals filed in three different offices
questions.explanation: If any tax period exceeds the threshold, a formal written protest is required for all periods involved.
questions.pageTitle: Request for Appeals consideration

questions.stem: Which is not a required element of a formal written protest?
options: The facts supporting the taxpayer's position on each disputed issue
The law or authority supporting the position on each disputed issue
A proposed settlement percentage
A penalties of perjury statement with a signature beneath it
questions.explanation: The protest states the taxpayer's position; it does not open with a number.
questions.pageTitle: Request for Appeals consideration

questions.stem: An enrolled agent submits a protest based entirely on figures supplied by the client's bookkeeper, which the agent has not verified. Which declaration is appropriate?
options: The taxpayer's own "to the best of my knowledge and belief" statement
The representative statement declaring no personal knowledge of the information stated
No declaration, because the representative did not prepare the underlying records
The representative statement declaring personal knowledge, since the agent prepared the protest
questions.explanation: Two representative statements exist precisely so that the declaration matches the practitioner's actual knowledge.
questions.pageTitle: Request for Appeals consideration

questions.stem: A client wants the protest to argue that federal income tax is unconstitutional. What should the representative advise?
options: Include it as an alternative argument; it costs nothing
Appeals cannot consider arguments based only on constitutional or similar objections
Appeals will refer the argument to Chief Counsel for a ruling
The argument must be made first in order to preserve it for court
questions.explanation: Appeals considers arguments based on tax law; moral, religious, political, constitutional and conscientious objections are outside what it may consider, and some are frivolous positions carrying a penalty.
questions.pageTitle: Request for Appeals consideration

questions.stem: Which statement about proceedings before Appeals is correct?
options: Testimony is taken under oath and transcribed
Proceedings are informal and no testimony under oath is taken
Only attorneys may appear
Proceedings follow the Federal Rules of Evidence
questions.explanation: Facts may be required in affidavits or declared true under penalties of perjury, but no oath is administered.
questions.pageTitle: Enrolled agent appearance at an Appeals conference

questions.stem: A taxpayer was offered an Appeals conference after a thirty-day letter and did not take it. After the notice of deficiency is mailed, what is the position?
options: A conference will be granted automatically on request
Ordinarily no conference will be granted in the 90-day status, absent unusual circumstances
Two further conferences are available as of right
The notice of deficiency is invalid for want of a conference
questions.explanation: The rule applies whether the conference was had or merely offered and declined.
questions.pageTitle: Enrolled agent appearance at an Appeals conference

questions.stem: A representative produces significant documents for the first time at a non-docketed Appeals conference. What may Appeals do?
options: Nothing; Appeals must consider whatever is presented
Transmit the documents to the examining function for consideration and comment, and return the
Refuse to consider the documents permanently
Impose a penalty on the representative
questions.explanation: A taxpayer cannot withhold evidence from the examining function and expect to introduce it for the first time at Appeals without risking the case being returned.
questions.pageTitle: Enrolled agent appearance at an Appeals conference

questions.stem: An Appeals officer recommends accepting the taxpayer's settlement proposal and a reviewing officer disapproves it. What is the taxpayer entitled to?
options: Automatic acceptance of the proposal
A conference with the reviewing officer, on written request
An immediate notice of deficiency
Referral to the Taxpayer Advocate Service
questions.explanation: unless the interest of the Government would be injured by the delay, as with an imminent limitations expiry.
questions.pageTitle: Enrolled agent appearance at an Appeals conference

questions.stem: When do the ex parte communication rules not apply?
options: During a collection due process hearing
When the taxpayer is unrepresented
To communications between Appeals and Counsel about a case docketed in the Tax Court
When the disputed amount is below the small case threshold
questions.explanation: The restriction targets communications that would compromise the independence of Appeals from the originating function; docketed-case communications with Counsel are outside it.
questions.pageTitle: Enrolled agent appearance at an Appeals conference

questions.stem: On what basis does Appeals settle a tax controversy?
options: The examiner's recommendation, adjusted for the taxpayer's ability to pay
The relative merits of the opposing views in light of the hazards of litigation
A fixed percentage of the proposed deficiency
Whatever amount the taxpayer offers in good faith
questions.explanation: Appeals prices the case by what would probably happen in court, not by re-auditing it.
questions.pageTitle: Settlement function of the Appeals process

questions.stem: A representative proposes a small payment on the footing that litigating would cost the Government more than the deficiency. How should Appeals respond?
options: Accept, since the analysis is economically sound
Refuse; no settlement may be based on the nuisance value of the case to either party
Refer the case to Counsel for a litigation cost estimate
Accept, but only with the examining function's consent
questions.explanation: The prohibition is symmetrical and protects taxpayers as well as the Government.
questions.pageTitle: Settlement function of the Appeals process

questions.stem: May Appeals raise an issue the examination never considered?
options: Never
Only with the taxpayer's written consent
Yes, if the ground is substantial and the effect on liability is material, after advising the
Yes, without restriction
questions.explanation: Appeals should also not reopen an issue on which the taxpayer and the examining function agreed, on the same test.
questions.pageTitle: Settlement function of the Appeals process

questions.stem: Appeals settles two of four issues in a case. What happens to the other two?
options: They are deemed conceded by the taxpayer
They are deemed conceded by the Government
A statutory notice of deficiency is prepared and issued for the unagreed issues
The whole case must go to the Tax Court
questions.explanation: The agreed issues are recorded on Form 870-AD and the unagreed issues carry a fresh 90-day petition period.
questions.pageTitle: Settlement function of the Appeals process

questions.stem: Which statement about Form 870-AD is correct?
options: It is a closing agreement under IRC § 7121 and is final and conclusive by statute
It waives restrictions on assessment and collection under an agreed settlement, and reflects
It preserves the right to petition the Tax Court on the issues it covers
It may be signed only by an attorney
questions.explanation: It is not a § 7121 closing agreement, though a disposition based on mutual concessions does bar a later technical advice request for that period.
questions.pageTitle: Settlement function of the Appeals process

questions.stem: What is the maximum period in which a taxpayer may petition the Tax Court after a notice of deficiency is mailed?
options: 30 days
60 days
90 days
150 days
questions.explanation: The ordinary period is 90 days; it is 150 days where the notice is addressed to a person outside the United States, so the maximum is 150.
questions.pageTitle: Issuance of the 90-day letter

questions.stem: What is the maximum amount of deficiency for any one taxable year for a case to qualify for the Tax Court small case procedure?
options: 20,000 dollars
30,000 dollars
50,000 dollars
100,000 dollars
questions.explanation: The ceiling applies to the amount of the deficiency placed in dispute, or any claimed overpayment, for any one taxable year.
questions.pageTitle: Issuance of the 90-day letter

questions.stem: While the petition period runs and before any petition is filed, what may the IRS do?
options: Assess the deficiency but not levy
Neither assess the deficiency nor levy or sue to collect it
Levy on wages but not on bank accounts
Assess and collect freely, since no petition has been filed
questions.explanation: Assessment, levy and collection proceedings are all prohibited until the period expires, and until any Tax Court decision becomes final if a petition is filed — jeopardy and termination assessments aside.
questions.pageTitle: Issuance of the 90-day letter

questions.stem: A taxpayer receives a notice stating that a mathematical error on the return produced additional tax, which has been assessed. May the taxpayer petition the Tax Court on that notice?
options: Yes, within 90 days of mailing
No; such a notice is expressly not a notice of deficiency for that purpose
Yes, but only if the amount exceeds the small case ceiling
Only after paying the additional tax
questions.explanation: The remedy is a request for abatement within the statutory window, which pushes the Service into deficiency procedures.
questions.pageTitle: Issuance of the 90-day letter

questions.stem: A taxpayer consents to rescission of a notice of deficiency. What is the effect on the assessment limitations period?
options: The suspension that ran while the notice was outstanding is undone
The period is suspended for a further 90 days
The suspension that ran while the rescinded notice was outstanding is unaffected
The period expires immediately on rescission
questions.explanation: Rescission removes the petition right and the further-deficiency-letter restriction, but expressly does not affect any suspension that already ran.
questions.pageTitle: Issuance of the 90-day letter

questions.stem: A preparer's software miscomputes a limitation and the resulting error is visible on the face of the return. Is the reasonable cause and good faith exception available?
options: Yes, because the error originated in the software
Yes, if the software vendor confirms the defect
No; the exception does not apply to an error that would have been apparent from a general review
Yes, provided the preparer installs the vendor's correction
questions.pageTitle: Reliance on software

questions.stem: On what may a preparer rely in good faith without verification?
options: The output of tax preparation software
Information furnished by the taxpayer, and information and advice furnished by another advisor or
Any figure appearing on a prior year return, without qualification
Nothing; every item must be independently verified
questions.explanation: The preparer is not required to audit or examine books and records to verify it.
questions.pageTitle: Reliance on software

questions.stem: When is reliance on another party's advice not in good faith?
options: Whenever the advice was given orally
Where the advice is unreasonable on its face, where the preparer knew or should have known the
Whenever the party works at the same firm as the preparer
Only where the party is not a credentialed practitioner
questions.explanation: Advice may be written or oral, though the burden of establishing it was received falls on the preparer.
questions.pageTitle: Reliance on software

questions.stem: What does Circular 230 § 10.22(b) presume?
options: That software output is accurate
That due diligence was exercised where the practitioner relied on the work product of another
That an isolated error is excusable
That a client's information is complete
questions.explanation: The presumption is about a person's work product, not a program's.
questions.pageTitle: Reliance on software

questions.stem: A firm makes the same computational error on numerous returns because an update was not installed. How does the reasonable cause exception apply?
options: It applies, because each error is individually minor
It applies, because the cause was external to the firm
It does not apply; the exception is withheld where the same or similar error is repeated on
It applies to the first ten returns only
questions.pageTitle: Reliance on software

questions.stem: A taxpayer receives a notice assessing additional tax because of a clerical error on the return. What may the taxpayer do?
options: Petition the Tax Court within 90 days
Request abatement within the statutory window, which puts the Service to deficiency procedures
Nothing; the assessment is final on issuance
Request an Appeals conference as of right before assessment
questions.explanation: The notice is expressly not a notice of deficiency, so no petition right attaches to it.
questions.pageTitle: Miscalculations and recognition of duplicate entries

questions.stem: Which is not within the statutory definition of a mathematical or clerical error?
options: An entry inconsistent with another entry on the same schedule
An omission of information required to substantiate an entry
A disputed valuation of donated property
A deduction exceeding a statutory limit expressed as a specified monetary amount, where the items
questions.explanation: A valuation dispute is a substantive disagreement requiring deficiency procedures.
questions.pageTitle: Miscalculations and recognition of duplicate entries

questions.stem: A preparer makes one inadvertent arithmetic error that is obvious on the face of the return. Does the reasonable cause and good faith exception apply?
options: Yes; isolated errors always qualify
Yes, provided the understatement is small
No, if the error is so obvious, flagrant or material that it should have been discovered during a
No; the exception never applies to arithmetic
questions.pageTitle: Miscalculations and recognition of duplicate entries

questions.stem: What does the regulation describe as a normal office practice?
options: Owning current tax preparation software
A system for promoting accuracy and consistency, generally including checklists, methods for
Employing at least one credentialed practitioner
Retaining returns for three years
questions.explanation: and the factor helps only where the practice was actually followed on the return in question.
questions.pageTitle: Miscalculations and recognition of duplicate entries

questions.stem: A duplicate entry causes a client's income to be overstated. What is the practical consequence?
options: The IRS will identify and correct it through a math error notice
The error is immaterial because no tax was understated
The client overpays, and only the firm's own review will find it
The reasonable cause exception makes it irrelevant
questions.explanation: Examination looks for understatements; nobody outside the firm is looking for this one.
questions.pageTitle: Miscalculations and recognition of duplicate entries

questions.stem: The retention period for a return increases from three years to six where omitted income exceeds what proportion of the gross income shown on the return?
options: 10 per cent
15 per cent
25 per cent
40 per cent
questions.explanation: It mirrors the substantial omission rule that extends the assessment period to six years.
questions.pageTitle: Length of time to retain returns and records

questions.stem: Which of these has no retention limit?
options: An ordinary tax return
A fraudulent return
Employment and payroll tax records
None of these
questions.explanation: Records should also be kept indefinitely where no return was filed; in both cases no assessment period ever begins to run.
questions.pageTitle: Length of time to retain returns and records

questions.stem: How long must employment tax records be kept?
options: Three years from the date the return was filed
At least four years after the date the tax becomes due or is paid, whichever is later
Six years from the end of the calendar year
Indefinitely
questions.pageTitle: Length of time to retain returns and records

questions.stem: A taxpayer received a building in a nontaxable exchange and later sells it. Which records must be retained until the limitations period for the year of sale expires?
options: Records on the replacement property only
Records on the relinquished property only
Records on both the relinquished and the replacement property
Neither, once three years have passed since the exchange
questions.explanation: Basis carried over, so the old property's records are needed to compute gain or loss.
questions.pageTitle: Length of time to retain returns and records

questions.stem: A taxpayer files a claim for refund two years after filing the original return and one year after paying an assessed balance. How long should the supporting records be kept?
options: Three years from the date the original return was filed
Two years from the date the tax was paid
The later of three years from filing the original return or two years from paying the tax
Seven years from the date of the claim
questions.explanation: The retention rule mirrors the claim period.
questions.pageTitle: Length of time to retain returns and records

questions.stem: Under what authority must a professional tax return preparer maintain a data security plan?
options: Circular 230 alone
The FTC Safeguards Rule, implementing the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, whose "financial institution"
State licensing boards only
It is a recommended practice with no legal basis
questions.explanation: Failure to create and enact a plan may result in an FTC investigation.
questions.pageTitle: Data security

questions.stem: Which firms must implement multi-factor authentication for access to customer information?
options: Firms with more than 50 employees
Firms that file more than 1,000 returns annually
All companies, regardless of size
Only Online Providers
questions.explanation: At least two of a knowledge factor, a possession factor and an inherence factor are required.
questions.pageTitle: Data security

questions.stem: A practitioner suspects client data may have been stolen but is not yet certain. What should happen?
options: Complete an internal investigation, then report if confirmed
Report the suspected data theft or loss immediately to the appropriate IRS Stakeholder Liaison
Notify only the affected clients
Nothing, unless fraudulent returns appear
questions.explanation: Reporting is not conditioned on certainty.
questions.pageTitle: Data security

questions.stem: Which is among the required elements of the information security plan?
options: Designating a qualified individual to oversee and enforce the programme
Purchasing cyber liability insurance
Retaining an outside auditor annually
Filing a copy of the plan with the IRS
questions.explanation: The plan must also include risk assessment, a monitored and tested safeguards programme, service provider oversight, periodic adjustment, and security awareness training.
questions.pageTitle: Data security

questions.stem: Which practice does Publication 4557 recommend specifically for detecting misuse of a firm's credentials?
options: Changing the EFIN annually
Checking e-file applications and PTIN accounts weekly for total returns filed
Filing Form 14039 for every client
Transmitting only through a third-party transmitter
questions.explanation: Unused EFINs should also be deactivated.
questions.pageTitle: Data security

questions.stem: An enrolled agent is listed as a Principal on an e-file application. What does the professional status information she provides replace?
options: The tax compliance check
The fingerprinting requirement
The criminal background check
The Terms of Agreement signature
questions.explanation: Attorneys, CPAs, enrolled agents, officers of publicly traded corporations and bonded bank officials provide credentials instead of being fingerprinted; every other check still applies.
questions.pageTitle: Application process to be an e-file provider

questions.stem: A practitioner sells her practice, including the client list and software. What happens to her EFIN?
options: It transfers to the buyer with the business
It may be leased to the buyer for one filing season
It does not transfer; the buyer must obtain its own EFIN from the IRS
It transfers if both parties notify the e-help Desk
questions.explanation: EFINs may not be transferred on a sale, gift or other disposition, and only the IRS may issue them.
questions.pageTitle: Application process to be an e-file provider

questions.stem: Which provider option cannot be selected on its own?
options: Electronic Return Originator
Transmitter
Online Provider
Software Developer
questions.explanation: Online Provider is a secondary role and must be paired with Software Developer, Transmitter or Intermediate Service Provider.
questions.pageTitle: Application process to be an e-file provider

questions.stem: Which is not among the enumerated grounds on which the IRS may deny participation in IRS e-file?
options: Failure to pay a state or local tax liability
Employing an individual expelled from participating in IRS e-file
Operating a practice with fewer than three employees
Stockpiling returns before acceptance to participate
questions.explanation: Firm size is not a criterion; the grounds are conduct, compliance and suitability based.
questions.pageTitle: Application process to be an e-file provider

questions.stem: A provider files no returns in either the current or the prior processing year. What follows?
options: Nothing; acceptance is permanent once granted
The IRS may notify the provider of removal, with a limited window to request reactivation
The provider must be fingerprinted again
The EFIN is automatically reassigned to another firm
questions.explanation: If the provider does not reply and request reactivation within the window, it must reapply.
questions.pageTitle: Application process to be an e-file provider

questions.stem: A preparer expects to file 8 individual income tax returns. She is a partner in a firm whose members expect to file 40 in total. She is:
options: Not a specified tax return preparer, being under the threshold
A specified tax return preparer, because the firm's members are aggregated
A specified tax return preparer only for returns she personally e-files
Exempt, as a firm member
questions.pageTitle: E-file mandate and exceptions (Form 8948)

questions.stem: To claim an administrative exemption under Notice 2011-26, a specified tax return preparer must:
options: File Form 8944 and await written approval
Do nothing to claim it, but be able to demonstrate entitlement on request
Attach Form 8944 to the taxpayer's return
Obtain a private letter ruling
questions.explanation: The exemptions are automatic.
questions.pageTitle: E-file mandate and exceptions (Form 8948)

questions.stem: A client wants to file on paper and mail the return himself. For the mandate not to apply, the preparer must obtain:
options: An oral instruction, noted in the file
A hand-signed, dated statement on or before the filing date, with the taxpayer submitting the return
Form 8948, signed by the taxpayer
An undue hardship waiver
questions.pageTitle: E-file mandate and exceptions (Form 8948)

questions.stem: A preparer's software does not support a schedule the return requires, so the return is filed on paper. The preparer should:
options: File Form 8944 before filing
Attach Form 8948 to the paper return, the exemption being automatic
Do nothing further
Request a private letter ruling
questions.explanation: This is a Notice 2011-26 paragraph B reason, and Form 8948's boxes track paragraphs A and B.
questions.pageTitle: E-file mandate and exceptions (Form 8948)

questions.stem: An undue hardship waiver request on Form 8944 must ordinarily be submitted:
options: At any time during the calendar year
With the first paper return filed
Between 1 October of the preceding year and 15 February of the applicable year
Within 30 days of the return's due date
questions.pageTitle: E-file mandate and exceptions (Form 8948)

questions.stem: Which mark may an Authorized IRS e-file Provider use in advertising?
options: The IRS insignia
The Department of the Treasury insignia
The IRS e-file logo
None of these
questions.explanation: used only to indicate that the provider offers or has performed the service, and never combined with the IRS eagle, the word "Federal," or other symbols suggesting a special relationship.
questions.pageTitle: Advertising standards

questions.stem: May a firm accepted into IRS e-file trade under the name "IRS Rapid Refunds"?
options: Yes, once accepted
Yes, if the IRS e-file logo also appears
No; a provider must not use "Internal Revenue Service" or "IRS" in its doing-business-as name
Yes, with e-help Desk approval
questions.explanation: The firm may describe itself as an Authorized IRS e-file Provider instead.
questions.pageTitle: Advertising standards

questions.stem: How must a refund anticipation loan be advertised?
options: As an accelerated refund
Clearly as a loan or other financial product, in easily readable print, making clear the taxpayer
Only in print media
It may not be advertised at all
questions.explanation: Describing the advance as the refund itself is the prohibited framing.
questions.pageTitle: Advertising standards

questions.stem: A provider's website carries words and logos outside the advertising rules. What may the IRS do?
options: Nothing; advertising is a consumer protection matter only
Assess a monetary penalty per impression
Temporarily inactivate the provider's e-file privileges until the advertising complies
Revoke the EFIN without notice or remedy
questions.explanation: It is an operational remedy aimed at getting the material fixed.
questions.pageTitle: Advertising standards

questions.stem: A provider advertises that returns can be e-filed using a client's final pay stub. Is this permitted?
options: Yes, if the W-2 follows within thirty days
Yes, for returning clients only
No; advertisements must not imply that Forms W-2, W-2G and 1099-R are unnecessary
Yes, if the taxpayer signs a waiver
questions.explanation: A provider is generally prohibited from e-filing before receiving those forms, and may not advertise otherwise.
questions.pageTitle: Advertising standards

questions.stem: What defines an Electronic Return Originator?
options: The provider that transmits return data directly to the IRS
The provider that begins the process of the electronic submission of a return
The provider that writes software to IRS specifications
Any paid preparer who signs a return
questions.explanation: Transmitting is the transmitter's role; an ERO may also be a transmitter but the roles are distinct provider options.
questions.pageTitle: Definition and responsibilities of an ERO

questions.stem: From whom may an ERO accept returns for origination?
options: Anyone willing to pay a per-return fee
Taxpayers and other Authorized IRS e-file Providers only
Any bookkeeping or payroll service
Any person holding a PTIN
questions.explanation: An ERO may originate only returns it prepared or collected from a taxpayer or another provider.
questions.pageTitle: Definition and responsibilities of an ERO

questions.stem: The IRS rejects the electronic portion of a return and the ERO cannot fix the reason. What must the ERO do?
options: Nothing until the taxpayer asks
File a paper return on the taxpayer's behalf without further contact
Take reasonable steps to inform the taxpayer within 24 hours, with the business rules and an
Resubmit the identical return up to three times
questions.explanation: A rejected return is considered not filed, so prompt notice is what preserves the taxpayer's options.
questions.pageTitle: Definition and responsibilities of an ERO

questions.stem: After the taxpayer signs the declaration, the ERO corrects the return so that total income rises by 90 dollars and total tax by 22 dollars. What is required?
options: Nothing; corrections may always be made before transmission
A new signed declaration from the taxpayer before retransmission
A paper return
Notification to the e-help Desk
questions.explanation: Both stated thresholds are exceeded, so the existing declaration no longer covers the return.
questions.pageTitle: Definition and responsibilities of an ERO

questions.stem: Which statement about providing a copy of the return is correct?
options: A paper printout is always required
A complete copy must be provided, in any medium acceptable to both taxpayer and ERO
The copy may omit documents that could not be transmitted electronically
A copy is required only if the taxpayer requests one
questions.explanation: A complete copy includes Form 8453 and other untransmittable documents along with the electronic portion.
questions.pageTitle: Definition and responsibilities of an ERO

questions.stem: How does the IRS categorise the seriousness of an e-file infraction?
options: By the dollar amount of tax involved
By Levels One, Two and Three, according to the adverse impact on the quality of electronically
By the number of returns the provider files annually
By whether the provider is an ERO or a transmitter
questions.pageTitle: Levels of infractions

questions.stem: A provider continues a Level One infraction after the IRS has brought it to the provider's attention. What is the result?
options: It remains a Level One infraction
It becomes a Level Two infraction
It becomes a Level Three infraction
It is disregarded if unintentional
questions.explanation: A continued Level Two after notice likewise becomes a Level Three.
questions.pageTitle: Levels of infractions

questions.stem: Which sanction cannot be appealed through the administrative review process?
options: An immediate suspension
A proposed expulsion
A written reprimand
A recommended suspension
questions.explanation: Reprimands carry no immediate consequence, so no review is available.
questions.pageTitle: Levels of infractions

questions.stem: A Level Three infraction involving identity theft is established. What may the IRS do?
options: Only issue a written reprimand pending review
Suspend or expel the provider before administrative review
Take no action until the administrative review is complete
Refer the matter to the Tax Court
questions.explanation: The IRS expressly reserves that right for Level Three infractions, and an immediate sanction remains in effect during the review.
questions.pageTitle: Levels of infractions

questions.stem: After how long may an individual expelled from IRS e-file be reconsidered?
options: One year
Two years
Five years from expulsion, or five years after completing rehabilitation
Never
questions.pageTitle: Levels of infractions

questions.stem: How often must an Authorized IRS e-file Provider reapply?
options: Every year
Every three years
Not at all, provided it continues to e-file and complies with suitability requirements
Whenever the EFIN prefix changes
questions.pageTitle: Compliance requirements to continue in the program

questions.stem: Which providers are excepted from the suitability check?
options: Sole proprietors
Those functioning solely as Software Developers
Providers filing fewer than 100 returns
Providers whose Principals are enrolled agents
questions.explanation: A Software Developer that also transmits is outside the exception.
questions.pageTitle: Compliance requirements to continue in the program

questions.stem: A firm adds a new Responsible Official mid-season. What is required?
options: Nothing until the next filing season
A notification e-mail to the e-help Desk
The e-file application must be resubmitted for processing
A new EFIN for the individual
questions.explanation: The new individual must also create an e-Services account and be fingerprinted unless they provide professional credentials.
questions.pageTitle: Compliance requirements to continue in the program

questions.stem: Which is not something the IRS may do during an e-file monitoring visit?
options: Scrutinise the provider's advertising material
Observe office and security procedures
Assess an immediate monetary penalty on the spot
Check tax compliance on the firm, Principals and Responsible Officials
questions.explanation: Monitoring gathers information; sanctions follow their own process.
questions.pageTitle: Compliance requirements to continue in the program

questions.stem: A Principal has an unpaid personal tax balance. What satisfies the tax compliance element of continuous suitability?
options: Nothing; any balance is disqualifying
Returns filed and the balance paid or covered by an installment agreement
A promise to pay before the next filing season
Filing the returns, regardless of the balance
questions.pageTitle: Compliance requirements to continue in the program

questions.stem: What is the first step for a provider that has been sanctioned and wishes to contest it?
options: A petition to the United States Tax Court
A written request for administrative review to the office that imposed the sanction
A written appeal directly to the Independent Office of Appeals
A complaint to the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration
questions.explanation: The appeal to the Independent Office of Appeals is the second step, available if the reviewing office upholds the sanction.
questions.pageTitle: EFIN revocation appeal process

questions.stem: By when must an administrative review or appeal be requested?
options: Within 10 calendar days of receiving the letter
Within 30 calendar days of the date of the denial or sanction letter
Within 60 days of receipt
There is no deadline
questions.explanation: Failure to request within that period terminates the right.
questions.pageTitle: EFIN revocation appeal process

questions.stem: What is the status of a suspension while the administrative review is pending?
options: It is stayed automatically
It is stayed if the provider posts a bond
It remains in effect
It is reduced to a written reprimand
questions.explanation: Neither a denial nor an immediate sanction is stayed by requesting review.
questions.pageTitle: EFIN revocation appeal process

questions.stem: A provider's participation is revoked because a federal court has enjoined its Principal from filing returns. What review is available?
options: The ordinary two-step administrative review
An appeal directly to the Independent Office of Appeals
None; the remedy is to reapply if the injunction expires or is reversed
Reconsideration after one year
questions.pageTitle: EFIN revocation appeal process

questions.stem: Which sanction cannot be taken through the administrative review process?
options: An immediate expulsion
A recommended suspension
A written reprimand
A proposed suspension
questions.explanation: Review and appeal are available for proposed, recommended or immediate suspensions and expulsions only.
questions.pageTitle: EFIN revocation appeal process

questions.stem: Which electronic signature method allows a completely paperless process?
options: The Self-Select PIN method
The Practitioner PIN method
Both methods
Neither method
questions.explanation: where the taxpayer enters their own PIN by keystroke after reviewing the return. The Practitioner PIN method always requires a signed authorization form.
questions.pageTitle: E-file authorization and supporting documentation

questions.stem: When must a taxpayer sign Form 8879 relative to transmission?
options: Within three days after the return is transmitted
Before the ERO originates the electronic submission of the return
At any time before the IRS acknowledges the return
Only if the IRS requests it
questions.explanation: The ERO may enter the PIN in the electronic record first, but the signature must precede origination.
questions.pageTitle: E-file authorization and supporting documentation

questions.stem: What does an ERO do with a signed Form 8879?
options: Mail it to the IRS with the return
Attach it to Form 8453
Retain it for three years from the later of the return due date or the IRS received date, and
Destroy it once the return is accepted
questions.pageTitle: E-file authorization and supporting documentation

questions.stem: A return claims a non-cash charitable contribution requiring a qualified appraisal that cannot be transmitted electronically. What is the correct handling?
options: Retain it in the client file; nothing is sent
Attach it to Form 8453 and mail it to the IRS, unless the software supports PDF attachment
Attach it to Form 8879
Mail it with a copy of the acknowledgment to the e-help Desk
questions.explanation: The ERO is responsible for submitting all paper documents required to complete the filing.
questions.pageTitle: E-file authorization and supporting documentation

questions.stem: Under the Practitioner PIN method, the taxpayer reviews the return and enters her own PIN by keystroke. Is a signature authorization form required?
options: No; entering her own PIN is the signature
No, provided the ERO documents that she entered it
Yes; the form is required even where the taxpayer enters her own PIN
Only if the return claims a refund
questions.explanation: The requirement is stated expressly and is what distinguishes the method from Self-Select.
questions.pageTitle: E-file authorization and supporting documentation

questions.stem: An individual return is transmitted on the due date and rejects. By when must the corrected return be resubmitted electronically to be treated as timely?
options: Two calendar days after the due date
Five calendar days after the due date
Ten calendar days after the due date
Thirty calendar days after the due date
questions.explanation: The return is then considered timely filed as of the original submission.
questions.pageTitle: Rejected returns and resolution

questions.stem: A corporation's e-filed return is rejected and cannot be corrected. When must the paper return be filed to be timely?
options: Within two days of the rejection
By the due date only, with no extension for the rejection
By the later of the due date including extensions, or ten calendar days after the last rejection
Within thirty days of the rejection
questions.explanation: and the filer must first contact the e-help Desk to attempt to resolve the reject.
questions.pageTitle: Rejected returns and resolution

questions.stem: Which is not a required element of a paper return filed to replace a rejected electronic return?
options: The rejected electronic return date written on the return
A copy of the rejection notification
A copy of the submission receipt
An explanation of why the return is being filed after the due date
questions.explanation: Retaining the submission receipt is a recommendation for the firm's records, not a required element of the paper return.
questions.pageTitle: Rejected returns and resolution

questions.stem: How long is an identity protection PIN valid?
options: For the taxpayer's lifetime
For one calendar year, with a new one generated each year
For three years following an identity theft report
Until the taxpayer changes address
questions.explanation: There is no fixed number of years after which the assignment stops.
questions.pageTitle: Rejected returns and resolution

questions.stem: What is the status of a return the IRS has rejected?
options: Filed, with processing suspended
Filed, but subject to correction
Not filed
Filed as of the date the rejection is resolved, in all cases
questions.explanation: It is treated as filed on the original date only if it is perfected within the applicable window.
questions.pageTitle: Rejected returns and resolution
